verses.text: Many have taken in hand (set out) to write in order an account. It is about those things which are most surely believed among us,
Even as they delivered (handed) them to us. They were eyewitnesses from the beginning, and ministers (servants) of the word.
It seemed good to me also to write to you in order, most excellent Theophilus. I have had perfect understanding of all things from the very first.
That you might know the certainty (sure truth) of those things in which you have been instructed (taught).

There was a certain priest named Zacharias, in the days of Herod, the king of Judaea. Zacharias was of the course (priest group) of Abia. His wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
And they were both righteous (right with God) before God. They walked in all the commandments and ordinances (rules) of the Lord blameless (without fault).
And they had no child, because Elisabeth was barren (not able to have children). They both were now well stricken in years (very old).
And it came to pass (happened) while Zacharias did the priest's work before God. He served in the order of his course (priest group).
It was according to the custom of the priest's office. His lot (chosen turn) was to burn incense (sweet-smelling spice) when he went into the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude (large crowd) of the people were praying outside at the time of incense (sweet-smelling spice).
And an angel of the Lord appeared to Zacharias. The angel stood on the right side of the altar of incense (sweet-smelling spice).
And when Zacharias saw the angel, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said to him: Fear not, Zacharias, for your prayer is heard. And your wife Elisabeth will bear you a son, and you will call his name John.
And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great in the sight of the Lord. John will drink neither wine nor strong drink. And he will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother's womb.
And many of the children of Israel will he turn to the Lord their God.

And John will go before Him in the spirit and power of Elias (Elijah). John will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children. And he will turn the disobedient to the wisdom of the just (those who are right with God). So John will make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
And Zacharias said to the angel: How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife well stricken in years (very old).
And the angel answering said to him: I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God. And I am sent to speak to you, and to show you these glad tidings (good news).

And look, you will be silent, and not able to speak. This will last until the day that these things are performed (done). It is because you do not believe my words. My words will be fulfilled (come true) in their season (time).
And the people waited for Zacharias, and marvelled (were amazed) that he tarried (stayed) so long in the temple.

And when Zacharias came out, he could not speak to them. And they perceived (understood) that he had seen a vision in the temple. For he beckoned (made signs) to them, and remained speechless (unable to speak).
And it came to pass (happened) when the days of his ministration (temple service) were finished. Then Zacharias departed to his own house.
And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived (became pregnant), and hid herself 5 months, saying:
The Lord has dealt with me this way. In these days He looked on me. He did this to take away my reproach (shame) among men.
And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God. Gabriel was sent to a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
To a virgin espoused (promised in marriage) to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David. And the virgin's name was Mary.
And the angel came in to her, and said: Hail (greetings), you who are highly favoured (shown great kindness), the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.
And when Mary saw the angel, she was troubled at his saying. She cast in her mind (wondered) what kind of salutation (greeting) this should be.
And the angel said to her: Fear not, Mary, for you have found favour with God.
And look, you will conceive (become pregnant) in your womb, and bring forth a Son. You will call His name JESUS.
He will be great, and will be called the Son of the Highest. And the Lord God will give to Him the throne of His father David.
And He will reign over the house of Jacob for ever. Of His kingdom there will be no end.
Then Mary said to the angel: How will this be, since I know not a man (I have never been with a man)?

And the angel answered and said to her: The Holy Spirit will come upon you. The power of the Highest will overshadow (cover) you. So that holy thing (holy Child) will be born of you. He will be called the Son of God.
And look, your cousin Elisabeth, she has also conceived (become pregnant with) a son in her old age. And this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren (not able to have children).
For with God nothing will be impossible.
And Mary said: Look, I am the handmaid (servant girl) of the Lord. Let it be to me according to your word. And the angel departed from her.
And Mary arose in those days. She went into the hill country with haste (quickly), into a city of Juda (Judah),
And entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted (greeted) Elisabeth.
And it came to pass (happened) when Elisabeth heard the salutation (greeting) of Mary. The babe (baby) leaped in her womb. And Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
And Elisabeth spoke out with a loud voice, and said: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
And why is this given to me? Why should the mother of my Lord come to me?
For look, the voice of your salutation (greeting) sounded in my ears. As soon as it did, the babe (baby) leaped in my womb for joy.
And blessed (happy) is she who believed. For there will be a performance (doing) of those things which were told her from the Lord.
And Mary said: My soul magnifies (praises) the Lord,
And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.
For He has regarded (looked upon) the low estate (lowly place) of His handmaiden (servant girl). For look, from now on all generations (people of all times) will call me blessed (happy).
For He who is mighty has done to me great things, and holy is His name.
And His mercy is on them who fear Him from generation to generation.
He has shown strength with His arm. He has scattered the proud in the imagination (thoughts) of their hearts.
He has put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted (lifted up) them of low degree (lowly people).
He has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich He has sent away empty.
He has holpen (helped) His servant Israel, in remembrance of His mercy,
As He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed (children) for ever.
And Mary abode (stayed) with Elisabeth about 3 months, and returned to her own house.
Now Elisabeth's full time came that she should be delivered (give birth). And she brought forth a son.
And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shown great mercy upon her. And they rejoiced with her.
And it came to pass (happened) on the 8th day that they came to circumcise (cut the foreskin of) the child. They called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
And his mother answered and said: Not so, but he will be called John.
And they said to her: There is none of your kindred (relatives) who is called by this name.
And they made signs to his father, to ask how he would have him called.
And Zacharias asked for a writing table (writing tablet), and wrote, saying: His name is John. And they all marvelled (were amazed).
And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed (set free). And he spoke, and praised God.
And fear came on all who dwelt (lived) round about them. And all these sayings were noised abroad (told all around) throughout all the hill country of Judaea.
And all they who heard them laid them up (kept them) in their hearts, saying: What kind of child will this be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.
And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit, and prophesied (spoke God's message), saying:
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He has visited and redeemed (bought back and set free) His people,
And He has raised up a horn (mighty power) of salvation (saving) for us. It is in the house of His servant David,
As He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets. They have been since the world began.
That we should be saved from our enemies. We should be saved from the hand of all who hate us.
To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember His holy agreement,
The oath (promise) which He swore to our father Abraham,
That He would grant this to us: That we, being delivered (rescued) out of the hand of our enemies, might serve Him without fear,
In holiness and righteousness (being right with God) before Him, all the days of our life.
And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Highest. For you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways,
To give knowledge of salvation (saving) to His people by the remission (forgiveness) of their sins,
This is through the tender mercy of our God. By it the dayspring (sunrise) from on high has visited us,
To give light to them who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death. To guide our feet into the way of peace.
And the child grew, and waxed (grew) strong in spirit. And he was in the deserts till the day of his showing to Israel.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened) in those days that a decree (order) went out from Caesar Augustus. It said that all the world should be taxed (listed for taxes).
And this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.
And all went to be taxed (listed for taxes), every one into his own city.

And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea. Joseph went to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. This was because he was of the house and lineage (family line) of David,
To be taxed (listed for taxes) with Mary his espoused (promised) wife, being great with child (far along in pregnancy).
And so it was, while they were there, the days were accomplished (completed). It was time for Mary to be delivered (give birth).
And Mary brought forth her firstborn Son. She wrapped Him in swaddling clothes (strips of cloth), and laid Him in a manger (animal feeding box). There was no room for them in the inn.
And there were shepherds in the same country. They were abiding (staying) in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
And look, the angel of the Lord came upon them. The glory of the Lord shone round about them. And they were sore (very) afraid.
And the angel said to them: Fear not. For look, I bring you good tidings (news) of great joy. It will be to all people.
For to you is born this day in the city of David a Savior. He is Christ the Lord.
And this will be a sign to you: You will find the babe (baby) wrapped in swaddling clothes (strips of cloth), lying in a manger (animal feeding box).
And suddenly a multitude (large crowd) of the heavenly host (army of angels) was with the angel. They were praising God, and saying:
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

And it came to pass (happened) when the angels had gone away from them into heaven. The shepherds said one to another: Let us now go even to Bethlehem. Let us see this thing which has come to pass (happened). The Lord has made it known to us.
And they came with haste (quickly). They found Mary, and Joseph, and the babe (baby) lying in a manger (animal feeding box).
And when they had seen it, they made known abroad the saying. It was what was told them about this Child.
And all who heard it wondered at the things the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered (thought deeply about) them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying (giving honor to) and praising God. They praised God for all the things that they had heard and seen. It was as it was told to them.

And 8 days were accomplished (completed) for the circumcising (cutting the foreskin) of the Child. Then His name was called JESUS. The angel had given Him this name before He was conceived in the womb.
And the days of Mary's purification (being made clean) were accomplished (completed) according to the law of Moses. Then they brought Jesus to Jerusalem, to present Him to the Lord,
As it is written in the law of the Lord: Every male that opens the womb (every firstborn son) will be called holy to the Lord,
And they came to offer a sacrifice. It was according to what is said in the law of the Lord: A pair of turtledoves (doves), or 2 young pigeons.

And look, there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon. And the same man was just (right with God) and devout (faithful to God), waiting for the consolation (comfort) of Israel. And the Holy Spirit was upon him.
And it was revealed (shown) to Simeon by the Holy Spirit. Simeon would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
And Simeon came by the Spirit into the temple. The parents brought in the Child Jesus. They came to do for Him after the custom of the law.
Then Simeon took Him up in his arms, and blessed God, and said:
Lord, now You let Your servant depart (die) in peace, according to Your word.
For my eyes have seen Your salvation (saving),
Which You have prepared before the face of all people,
A light to lighten the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and the glory of Your people Israel.
And Joseph and His mother marvelled (were amazed) at those things which were spoken of Him.
And Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary His mother: Look, this Child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel. He is set for a sign which will be spoken against.
Yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul also. This is so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed (shown).

And there was one Anna, a prophetess (woman who spoke God's message). She was the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser (Asher). She was of a great age. She had lived with a husband 7 years from her virginity (after she married).
And she was a widow of about 84 years. She did not depart from the temple. She served God with fastings (going without food) and prayers night and day.
And Anna came in at that instant, and gave thanks likewise to the Lord. She spoke of Him to all those who looked for redemption (being bought back and set free) in Jerusalem.
And they performed all things according to the law of the Lord. Then they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.
And the Child grew, and waxed (grew) strong in spirit, filled with wisdom. And the grace of God was upon Him.
Now His parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover (feast of freedom from Egypt).
And when Jesus was 12 years old, they went up to Jerusalem. They went after the custom of the feast.
And they fulfilled (finished) the days. As they returned, the Child Jesus tarried (stayed) behind in Jerusalem. And Joseph and His mother did not know of it.
But they, supposing Him to have been in the company (group of travelers), went a day's journey. And they sought (looked for) Him among their kinsfolk (relatives) and acquaintance (friends).
And when they did not find Him, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking (looking for) Him.
And it came to pass (happened) after 3 days that they found Him in the temple. He was sitting in the middle of the doctors (teachers of the law). He was both hearing them, and asking them questions.
And all who heard Him were astonished (amazed) at His understanding and answers.
And when they saw Him, they were amazed. And His mother said to Him: Son, why have You dealt with us like this? Look, Your father and I have sought (looked for) You sorrowing (full of worry).
And Jesus said to them: How is it that you sought (looked for) Me? Did you not know that I must be about My Father's business?
And they did not understand the saying which He spoke to them.
And Jesus went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject (obedient) to them. But His mother kept all these sayings in her heart.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature (height), and in favour with God and man.

verses.text: Now it was the 15th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar. Pontius Pilate was governor of Judaea. Herod was tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) of Galilee. His brother Philip was tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis. Lysanias was the tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) of Abilene.
Annas and Caiaphas were the high priests. Then the word of God came to John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness (desert).
And John came into all the country about Jordan. John preached the baptism of repentance (a change of heart) for the remission (forgiveness) of sins,
As it is written in the book of the words of Esaias (Isaiah) the prophet, saying: The voice of one crying in the wilderness (desert): Prepare the way of the Lord, make His paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. And the crooked will be made straight, and the rough ways will be made smooth.
And all flesh (all people) will see the salvation (saving) of God.

Then John said to the multitude (large crowd) that came forth to be baptized by him: O generation of vipers (children of poisonous snakes), who has warned you to flee (run away) from the wrath (God's anger) to come?

So bring forth fruits worthy of repentance (a change of heart). Do not begin to say within yourselves: We have Abraham as our father. For I say to you: God is able of these stones to raise up children to Abraham.
And now also the axe is laid to the root of the trees. So every tree which does not bring forth good fruit is hewn (cut) down. It is cast into the fire.
And the people asked John, saying: What will we do then?
John answers and says to them: The one who has 2 coats, let them impart (share) with the one who has none. And the one who has meat (food), let them do likewise.
Then publicans (tax collectors) also came to be baptized, and said to John: Master (Teacher), what will we do?
And John said to them: Exact (collect) no more than that which is appointed (set) for you.
And the soldiers likewise demanded of John, saying: And what will we do? And John said to them: Do violence to no man, neither accuse any falsely. And be content with your wages (pay).
And the people were in expectation. All men mused (wondered) in their hearts about John. They wondered whether he was the Christ, or not.

John answered, saying to them all: I indeed baptize you with water. But One mightier than I comes. I am not worthy to unloose (untie) the latchet (strap) of His shoes. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

His fan (winnowing tool) is in His hand. He will throughly purge (completely clean) His floor, and will gather the wheat into His garner (barn). But the chaff (husks) He will burn with fire unquenchable (that cannot be put out).
And many other things in his exhortation (encouraging) John preached to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) was reproved (corrected) by John. It was for Herodias his brother Philip's wife. It was also for all the evils which Herod had done.
Herod added yet this above all: he shut up John in prison.
Now all the people were baptized. And it came to pass (happened) that Jesus also was baptized. As Jesus was praying, the heaven was opened,
And the Holy Spirit descended (came down) in a bodily shape like a dove upon Him. And a voice came from heaven, which said: You are My beloved (dearly loved) Son. In You I am well pleased.
And Jesus Himself began to be about 30 years of age. He was, as was supposed (thought), the son of Joseph. Joseph was the son of Heli,
Who was the son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi, who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Janna, who was the son of Joseph,
Who was the son of Mattathias, who was the son of Amos, who was the son of Naum, who was the son of Esli, who was the son of Nagge,
Who was the son of Maath, who was the son of Mattathias, who was the son of Semei, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Juda,
Who was the son of Joanna, who was the son of Rhesa, who was the son of Zorobabel (Zerubbabel), who was the son of Salathiel, who was the son of Neri,
Who was the son of Melchi, who was the son of Addi, who was the son of Cosam, who was the son of Elmodam, who was the son of Er,
Who was the son of Jose, who was the son of Eliezer, who was the son of Jorim, who was the son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi,
Who was the son of Simeon, who was the son of Juda, who was the son of Joseph, who was the son of Jonan, who was the son of Eliakim,
Who was the son of Melea, who was the son of Menan, who was the son of Mattatha, who was the son of Nathan, who was the son of David,
Who was the son of Jesse, who was the son of Obed, who was the son of Booz (Boaz), who was the son of Salmon, who was the son of Naasson (Nahshon),
Who was the son of Aminadab, who was the son of Aram, who was the son of Esrom (Hezron), who was the son of Phares (Perez), who was the son of Juda (Judah),
Who was the son of Jacob, who was the son of Isaac, who was the son of Abraham, who was the son of Thara (Terah), who was the son of Nachor (Nahor),
Who was the son of Saruch (Serug), who was the son of Ragau (Reu), who was the son of Phalec (Peleg), who was the son of Heber, who was the son of Sala,
Who was the son of Cainan, who was the son of Arphaxad, who was the son of Sem (Shem), who was the son of Noe (Noah), who was the son of Lamech,
Who was the son of Mathusala (Methuselah), who was the son of Enoch, who was the son of Jared, who was the son of Maleleel, who was the son of Cainan,
Who was the son of Enos, who was the son of Seth, who was the son of Adam, who was the son of God.
And Jesus, being full of the Holy Spirit, returned from Jordan. He was led by the Spirit into the wilderness (desert),
Being 40 days tempted (tested) by the devil. And in those days Jesus ate nothing. And when they were ended, He afterward hungered.
And the devil said to Him: If You are the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.
And Jesus answered him, saying: It is written that man will not live by bread alone. Man will live by every word of God.
And the devil took Jesus up into a high mountain. The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.
And the devil said to Him: All this power will I give You, and the glory of them. For that is delivered (handed over) to me, and to whomever I will, I give it.
If You therefore will worship me, all will be Yours.
And Jesus answered and said to him: Get behind Me, Satan. For it is written: You will worship the Lord your God, and Him only will you serve.
And the devil brought Jesus to Jerusalem, and set Him on a pinnacle (high point) of the temple. The devil said to Him: If You are the Son of God, cast Yourself down from here.
For it is written: He will give His angels charge (orders) over You, to keep You,
And in their hands they will bear You up. Then at no time will You dash (strike) Your foot against a stone.
And Jesus answering said to him: It is said: You will not tempt (test) the Lord your God.
And the devil had ended all the temptation (testing). Then he departed from Jesus for a season (a while).
And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee. And there went out a fame (news) of Him through all the region round about.
And Jesus taught in their synagogues (meeting houses), being glorified (praised) by all.
And Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As His custom was, He went into the synagogue (meeting house) on the sabbath day (day of rest). And He stood up to read.
And there was delivered (handed) to Him the book of the prophet Esaias (Isaiah). And when Jesus had opened the book, He found the place where it was written:

The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me. He has anointed (chosen and set apart) Me to preach the gospel (good news) to the poor. He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted. He sent Me to preach deliverance (freedom) to the captives (prisoners). He sent Me to preach recovering of sight to the blind. He sent Me to set at liberty (free) them who are bruised (crushed),
To preach the acceptable (welcome) year of the Lord.
And Jesus closed the book, and gave it again to the minister (servant), and sat down. The eyes of all those who were in the synagogue (meeting house) were fastened (fixed) on Him.
And Jesus began to say to them: This day is this scripture fulfilled (come true) in your ears.
And all bare Him witness (spoke well of Him). They wondered at the gracious words which came out of His mouth. And they said: Is this not Joseph's son?
And Jesus said to them: You will surely say to Me this proverb (saying): Physician (doctor), heal Yourself. Whatever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in Your country (hometown).
And Jesus said: Verily (truly) I say to you: No prophet is accepted in their own country (hometown).
But I tell you of a truth: Many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias (Elijah). The heaven was shut up 3 years and 6 months. Great famine (hunger) was throughout all the land.
But Elias (Elijah) was sent to none of them. He was sent only to Sarepta, a city of Sidon. He was sent to a woman who was a widow.
And many lepers (people with a skin disease) were in Israel in the time of Eliseus (Elisha) the prophet. And none of them was cleansed (healed), except Naaman the Syrian.
And all those in the synagogue (meeting house) heard these things. They were filled with wrath (great anger),
And they rose up, and thrust Jesus out of the city. They led Him to the brow (edge) of the hill on which their city was built. They wanted to cast Him down headlong.
But Jesus, passing through the middle of them, went His way,
And Jesus came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee. He taught them on the sabbath days (days of rest).
And they were astonished (amazed) at His doctrine (teaching), for His word was with power.
And in the synagogue (meeting house) was a man with a spirit of an unclean devil (demon). The man cried out with a loud voice,
Saying: Let us alone. What have we to do with You, You Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know You, who You are, the Holy One of God.

And Jesus rebuked (gave a strong command to) the demon, saying: Hold your peace (be quiet), and come out of him. The devil (demon) threw the man in the middle. Then it came out of him, and did not hurt him.
And they were all amazed, and spoke among themselves, saying: What a word this is. For with authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.
And the fame (news) of Jesus went out into every place of the country round about.
And Jesus arose out of the synagogue (meeting house), and entered into Simon's house. And Simon's wife's mother was taken with a great fever. And they besought (begged) Jesus for her.
And Jesus stood over her, and rebuked (gave a strong command to) the fever, and it left her. And immediately she arose and ministered to (served) them.
Now the sun was setting. All those who had any sick with divers (many different) diseases brought them to Jesus. And He laid His hands on every one of them, and healed them.
And devils (demons) also came out of many, crying out, and saying: You are Christ the Son of God. And Jesus, rebuking them, suffered (allowed) them not to speak, for they knew that He was Christ.
And when it was day, Jesus departed and went into a desert place. The people sought (looked for) Him, and came to Him. They stayed (held on to) Him, so that He would not depart from them.
And Jesus said to them: I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also. For that is why I am sent.
And Jesus preached in the synagogues (meeting houses) of Galilee.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened) that the people pressed upon Jesus. They wanted to hear the word of God. Jesus stood by the lake of Gennesaret,
And saw 2 ships (boats) standing by the lake. But the fishermen had gone out of them, and were washing their nets.
And Jesus entered into one of the ships (boats), which was Simon's. Jesus prayed (asked) Simon to thrust out a little from the land. And Jesus sat down, and taught the people out of the ship.
Now when Jesus had left speaking, He said to Simon: Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught (catch of fish).
And Simon answering said to Him: Master (Teacher), we have toiled (worked hard) all the night, and have taken nothing. Nevertheless (but) at Your word I will let down the net.
And when they had done this, they inclosed (caught) a great multitude (number) of fishes. And their net broke.
And they beckoned (waved) to their partners, who were in the other ship (boat). They wanted them to come and help them. And they came, and filled both the ships, so that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus' knees, saying: Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.
For Peter was astonished (amazed), and all who were with him. They were amazed at the draught (catch) of the fishes which they had taken.
And so also were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon: Fear not. From now on you will catch men.
And when they had brought their ships (boats) to land, they forsook (left) all, and followed Jesus.

And it came to pass (happened) when Jesus was in a certain city. Look, there was a man full of leprosy (skin disease). Seeing Jesus, the man fell on his face, and besought (begged) Him. He said: Lord, if You will, You can make me clean.
And Jesus put forth His hand, and touched him, saying: I will. Be clean. And immediately the leprosy (skin disease) departed from him.
And Jesus charged (strongly told) him to tell no man. Jesus said: But go, and show yourself to the priest. Offer for your cleansing, according as Moses commanded, for a testimony (proof) to them.
But so much the more a fame (news) of Jesus went abroad. And great multitudes (large crowds) came together to hear. They came to be healed by Him of their infirmities (sicknesses).
And Jesus withdrew Himself into the wilderness (desert), and prayed.

And it came to pass (happened) on a certain day, as Jesus was teaching. There were Pharisees and doctors of the law (teachers of the law) sitting by. They had come out of every town of Galilee, and Judaea, and Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them.
And look, men brought in a bed a man who was taken with a palsy (could not move his body). And they sought (looked for a) means to bring him in, and to lay him before Jesus.

And they could not find a way to bring him in because of the multitude (large crowd). So they went upon the housetop. They let him down through the tiling (roof tiles) with his couch, into the middle before Jesus.
And when Jesus saw their faith, He said to him: Man, your sins are forgiven you.
And the scribes (teachers of the law) and the Pharisees began to reason, saying: Who is this who speaks blasphemies (words against God)? Who can forgive sins, but God alone?
But when Jesus perceived (knew) their thoughts, He answering said to them: What do you reason (think) in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say: Your sins are forgiven you? Or to say: Rise up and walk?

But I want you to know this: The Son of man has power upon earth to forgive sins. Then Jesus said to the man sick of the palsy (who could not move his body): I say to you, Arise (get up). Take up your couch, and go into your house.
And immediately the man rose up before them, and took up that on which he lay. He departed to his own house, glorifying (praising) God.
And they were all amazed, and they glorified (praised) God, and were filled with fear, saying: We have seen strange things today.
And after these things Jesus went forth. He saw a publican (tax collector), named Levi, sitting at the receipt of custom (tax booth). And Jesus said to him: Follow Me.
And Levi left all, rose up, and followed Jesus.
And Levi made Jesus a great feast in his own house. And there was a great company of publicans (tax collectors) and of others who sat down with them.
But their scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees murmured (complained) against His disciples, saying: Why do you eat and drink with publicans (tax collectors) and sinners?
And Jesus answering said to them: They who are whole (healthy) do not need a physician (doctor), but they who are sick.
I came not to call the righteous (those right with God), but sinners to repentance (a change of heart).
And they said to Jesus: Why do the disciples of John fast (go without food) often, and make prayers? The disciples of the Pharisees do the same. But Yours eat and drink.
And Jesus said to them: Can you make the children of the bridechamber (friends of the bridegroom) fast (go without food), while the bridegroom (the man getting married) is with them?
But the days will come when the bridegroom (the man getting married) will be taken away from them. Then they will fast (go without food) in those days.

And Jesus spoke also a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them: No man puts a piece of a new garment (clothes) upon an old. If he does, then the new makes a rent (tear). And the piece that was taken out of the new does not agree with the old.
And no man puts new wine into old bottles (leather wine bags). Or else the new wine will burst the bottles (leather wine bags). It will be spilled, and the bottles will perish (be ruined).
But new wine must be put into new bottles (leather wine bags), and both are preserved (kept safe).
No man also having drunk old wine straightway (right away) desires new. For he says: The old is better.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened) on the second sabbath after the first. Jesus went through the corn (grain) fields. And His disciples plucked the ears of corn (heads of grain), and ate, rubbing them in their hands.
And certain of the Pharisees said to them: Why do you that which is not lawful (allowed by the law) to do on the sabbath days (days of rest)?
And Jesus answering them said: Have you not read so much as this? Have you not read what David did when he himself was hungry, and those with him?

David went into the house of God, and took and ate the shewbread (holy bread set before God). He gave also to those who were with him. It is not lawful (allowed by the law) to eat it, except for the priests alone.
And Jesus said to them: The Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath (day of rest).

And it came to pass (happened) also on another sabbath (day of rest). Jesus entered into the synagogue (meeting house) and taught. And there was a man whose right hand was withered (dried up and useless).
And the scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees watched Jesus. They watched whether He would heal on the sabbath day (day of rest). They wanted to find an accusation against Him.
But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to the man who had the withered (dried up) hand: Rise up, and stand forth in the middle. And the man arose and stood forth.
Then Jesus said to them: I will ask you one thing: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) on the sabbath days (days of rest) to do good, or to do evil? To save life, or to destroy it?
And looking round about upon them all, Jesus said to the man: Stretch forth your hand. And the man did so. And his hand was restored whole (healed) as the other.
And they were filled with madness (great anger). They communed (talked) one with another about what they might do to Jesus.
And it came to pass (happened) in those days. Jesus went out into a mountain to pray. He continued all night in prayer to God.
And when it was day, Jesus called to Him His disciples. And of them He chose 12, whom also He named apostles (sent ones):
Simon, whom He also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes (the Zealot),
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, who also was the traitor.

And Jesus came down with them, and stood in the plain (flat land). The company of His disciples was there. A great multitude (large crowd) of people was there out of all Judaea and Jerusalem. They came from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon. They came to hear Him, and to be healed of their diseases,
And they who were vexed (troubled) with unclean spirits. And they were healed.
And the whole multitude (large crowd) sought (tried) to touch Jesus. For there went virtue (power) out of Him, and healed them all.
And Jesus lifted up His eyes on His disciples, and said: Blessed are you poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

Blessed are you, when men will hate you. Blessed are you when they separate you from their company. Blessed are you when they reproach (insult) you, and cast out your name as evil. This is for the Son of man's sake.
Rejoice in that day, and leap for joy. For look, your reward is great in heaven. For in the same way their fathers did to the prophets.
But woe (great trouble) to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation (comfort).
Woe (great trouble) to you who are full, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.
Woe (great trouble) to you, when all men will speak well of you. For so did their fathers to the false prophets.
But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to them who hate you,
Bless them who curse you, and pray for them who despitefully use (mistreat) you.
And to the one who smites (strikes) you on the one cheek, offer also the other. Someone may take away your cloke (coat). Do not forbid them to take your coat also.
Give to every man who asks of you. And of the one who takes away your goods, do not ask them again.
And as you would want men to do to you, you also do to them likewise.
For if you love them who love you, what thank (credit) do you have? For sinners also love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what thank (credit) have you? For sinners also do even the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what thank (credit) have you? For sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.
But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again. And your reward will be great, and you will be the children of the Highest. For He is kind to the unthankful and to the evil.
Be therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.
Judge not, and you will not be judged. Condemn (judge guilty) not, and you will not be condemned (judged guilty). Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

Give, and it will be given to you. Good measure will men give into your bosom (lap). It will be pressed down, and shaken together, and running over. For with the same measure that you mete (measure out), it will be measured to you again.
And Jesus spoke a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them: Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into the ditch?
The disciple is not above their master (teacher). But every one who is perfect (fully trained) will be as their master (teacher).
And why do you behold (see) the mote (speck of dust) that is in your brother's eye? Why do you not perceive (notice) the beam (big piece of wood) that is in your own eye?

Or how can you say to your brother: Brother, let me pull out the mote (speck of dust) that is in your eye? You yourself do not see the beam (big piece of wood) that is in your own eye. You hypocrite (pretender), cast out first the beam (big piece of wood) out of your own eye. Then you will see clearly to pull out the mote (speck of dust) that is in your brother's eye.
For a good tree does not bring forth corrupt (rotten) fruit. Neither does a corrupt (rotten) tree bring forth good fruit.
For every tree is known by its own fruit. For men do not gather figs of thorns. Nor do they gather grapes of a bramble bush (thorn bush).

A good person brings forth good out of the good treasure of their heart. And an evil person brings forth evil out of the evil treasure of their heart. For out of the abundance (overflow) of the heart their mouth speaks.
And why do you call Me: Lord, Lord, and do not do the things which I say?
Whoever comes to Me, and hears My sayings, and does them: I will show you whom they are like.

They are like a man who built a house. He dug deep, and laid the foundation on a rock. The flood arose, and the stream beat vehemently (hard) upon that house. But it could not shake it, for it was founded upon a rock.

But the one who hears and does not do is like a man. That man built a house upon the earth without a foundation. Against it the stream beat vehemently (hard), and immediately it fell. And the ruin of that house was great.

verses.text: Now Jesus had ended all His sayings in the audience (hearing) of the people. Then He entered into Capernaum.
And a certain centurion's (army officer's) servant, who was dear to him, was sick, and ready to die.
And the centurion (army officer) heard of Jesus. He sent to Jesus the elders of the Jews. They besought (begged) Jesus to come and heal his servant.
And they came to Jesus, and besought (begged) Him instantly (earnestly). They said that the centurion (army officer) was worthy for Jesus to do this.
For he loves our nation, and he has built us a synagogue (meeting house).

Then Jesus went with them. He was now not far from the house. Then the centurion (army officer) sent friends to Him, saying to Him: Lord, do not trouble Yourself. For I am not worthy that You should enter under my roof.
That is why I did not think myself worthy to come to You. But say in a word, and my servant will be healed.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers. And I say to one: Go, and he goes. And to another: Come, and he comes. And to my servant: Do this, and he does it.
When Jesus heard these things, He marvelled (was amazed) at him. He turned around, and said to the people who followed Him: I say to you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And those who were sent returned to the house. They found the servant whole (healed) who had been sick.
And it came to pass (happened) the day after, that Jesus went into a city called Nain. And many of His disciples went with Him, and many people.
Now Jesus came nigh (near) to the gate of the city. Look, there was a dead man carried out. He was the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. And many people of the city were with her.
And when the Lord saw her, He had compassion (deep pity) on her, and said to her: Weep not.
And Jesus came and touched the bier (stretcher for the dead). And they who carried him stood still. And Jesus said: Young man, I say to you: Arise (get up).
And he who was dead sat up, and began to speak. And Jesus delivered (gave) him to his mother.
And there came a fear on all. And they glorified (praised) God, saying: A great prophet has risen up among us. And: God has visited His people.
And this rumour (report) of Jesus went forth throughout all Judaea. It went throughout all the region round about.
And the disciples of John showed him of all these things.
And John, calling to him 2 of his disciples, sent them to Jesus, saying: Are You He who should come? Or do we look for another?
When the men had come to Jesus, they said: John the Baptist has sent us to You, saying: Are You He who should come? Or do we look for another?
And in that same hour Jesus cured many of their infirmities (sicknesses) and plagues (diseases). He cured many of evil spirits. And to many who were blind He gave sight.

Then Jesus answering said to them: Go your way, and tell John what things you have seen and heard. The blind see, the lame (people who cannot walk well) walk. The lepers (people with a skin disease) are cleansed (healed), the deaf hear. The dead are raised. To the poor the gospel (good news) is preached.
And blessed (happy) is anyone who will not be offended in Me (turn away because of Me).
And the messengers of John had departed. Then Jesus began to speak to the people about John: What did you go out into the wilderness (desert) to see? A reed (tall grass) shaken with the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man clothed in soft raiment (clothes)? Look, they who are gorgeously apparelled (dressed), and live delicately (in comfort), are in kings' courts.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and much more than a prophet.
This is he of whom it is written: Look, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.
For I say to you: Among those born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist. But the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
And all the people who heard Jesus, and the publicans (tax collectors), justified God (said God was right). They had been baptized with the baptism of John.
But the Pharisees and lawyers (experts in God's law) rejected the counsel (plan) of God against themselves. They had not been baptized by John.
And the Lord said: To what then will I liken (compare) the men of this generation (people living now)? And what are they like?

They are like children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying: We have piped (played the flute) to you, and you have not danced. We have mourned (cried) to you, and you have not wept.
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say: He has a devil (demon).
The Son of man has come eating and drinking, and you say: Look, a gluttonous (eats too much) man, and a winebibber (drinks too much wine), a friend of publicans (tax collectors) and sinners.
But wisdom is justified (shown to be right) by all her children.
And one of the Pharisees desired (asked) Jesus that He would eat with him. And Jesus went into the Pharisee's house, and sat down to meat (to eat a meal).

And look, there was a woman in the city who was a sinner. She knew that Jesus sat at meat (ate a meal) in the Pharisee's house. So she brought an alabaster box (a stone jar) of ointment (perfumed oil).

She stood at His feet behind Him weeping. She began to wash His feet with tears. She wiped them with the hairs of her head. She kissed His feet, and anointed (put oil on) them with the ointment (perfumed oil).

Now the Pharisee who had bidden (invited) Jesus saw it. He spoke within himself, saying: If this man were a prophet, He would have known what kind of woman this is. He would know who touches Him, for she is a sinner.
And Jesus answering said to him: Simon, I have something to say to you. And Simon says: Master (Teacher), say on.
There was a certain creditor (lender) who had 2 debtors (people who owed him money). The one owed 500 pence (small coins), and the other 50.
And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly (freely) forgave them both. Tell Me therefore, which of them will love him most?
Simon answered and said: I suppose that he to whom he forgave most. And Jesus said to him: You have rightly judged.

And Jesus turned to the woman, and said to Simon: Do you see this woman? I entered into your house, and you gave Me no water for My feet. But she has washed My feet with tears. She has wiped them with the hairs of her head.
You gave Me no kiss. But this woman, since the time I came in, has not ceased (stopped) to kiss My feet.
My head with oil you did not anoint (put oil on). But this woman has anointed My feet with ointment (perfumed oil).
That is why I say to you: Her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.
And Jesus said to her: Your sins are forgiven.
And they who sat at meat (ate) with Him began to say within themselves: Who is this who forgives sins also?
And Jesus said to the woman: Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened) afterward that Jesus went throughout every city and village. He was preaching and showing the glad tidings (good news) of the kingdom of God. And the 12 were with Him,
And certain women, who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities (sicknesses): Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went 7 devils (demons),
And Joanna the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward (manager), and Susanna were with Him. Many others were too, who ministered to (served) Him of their substance (money and goods).
And many people were gathered together, and had come to Jesus out of every city. Then He spoke by a parable (story that teaches a lesson):

A sower (a man planting seed) went out to sow (plant) his seed. And as he sowed, some fell by the way side (along the path). And it was trodden down, and the fowls (birds) of the air devoured (ate) it.
And some fell upon a rock. And as soon as it was sprung up, it withered (dried up) away, because it lacked moisture.
And some fell among thorns. And the thorns sprang up with it, and choked it.
And other seed fell on good ground, and sprang up, and bore fruit a hundredfold (100 times as much). And when Jesus had said these things, He cried: Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
And His disciples asked Him, saying: What might this parable (story that teaches a lesson) be?

And Jesus said: To you it is given to know the mysteries (secrets) of the kingdom of God. But to others it is given in parables (stories that teach a lesson). So seeing they might not see, and hearing they might not understand.
Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of God.
Those by the way side (along the path) are those who hear. Then the devil comes, and takes away the word out of their hearts. He does this so that they would not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are those who receive the word with joy when they hear. And these have no root. They believe for a while, and in time of temptation (testing) fall away.
And that which fell among thorns are those who have heard and go forth. They are choked with cares (worries) and riches and pleasures of this life. They bring no fruit to perfection (to full growth).
But that on the good ground are those with an honest and good heart. Having heard the word, they keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
No man lights a candle (lamp) and covers it with a vessel (jar). No man puts it under a bed. But he sets it on a candlestick (lamp stand). Then those who enter in may see the light.
For nothing is secret, that will not be made manifest (shown openly). Neither anything hidden, that will not be known and come abroad (out in the open).
Take heed (be careful) therefore how you hear. For whoever has, to them will be given. And whoever has not, from them will be taken even that which they seem to have.
Then His mother and His brothers came to Jesus. They could not come near Him for the press (crowd).
And it was told Him by certain people who said: Your mother and Your brothers stand outside, desiring (wanting) to see You.
And Jesus answered and said to them: My mother and My brothers are these who hear the word of God, and do it.
Now it came to pass (happened) on a certain day. Jesus went into a ship (boat) with His disciples. And He said to them: Let us go over to the other side of the lake. And they launched forth.
But as they sailed Jesus fell asleep. And there came down a storm of wind on the lake. And they were filled with water, and were in jeopardy (danger).

And they came to Jesus, and awoke Him, saying: Master, Master, we perish (are dying). Then Jesus arose, and rebuked (gave a strong command to) the wind and the raging of the water. And they ceased (stopped), and there was a calm.
And Jesus said to them: Where is your faith? And they, being afraid, wondered, saying one to another: What kind of man is this? For He commands even the winds and water, and they obey Him.
And they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against (across from) Galilee.
And Jesus went forth to land. There met Him out of the city a certain man, who had devils (demons) a long time. He wore no clothes. He did not abide (stay) in any house, but in the tombs.
When the man saw Jesus, he cried out, and fell down before Him. With a loud voice he said: What have I to do with You, Jesus, You Son of God most high? I beseech (beg) You, torment (hurt) me not.

For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For often it had caught him. And he was kept bound with chains and in fetters (leg chains). And he broke the bands, and was driven by the devil (demon) into the wilderness (desert).
And Jesus asked him, saying: What is your name? And he said: Legion (an army of thousands), because many devils (demons) had entered into him.
And they besought (begged) Jesus not to command them to go out into the deep (bottomless pit).
And there was there a herd of many swine (pigs) feeding on the mountain. And the demons besought (begged) Jesus that He would suffer (allow) them to enter into them. And He suffered (allowed) them.
Then the devils (demons) went out of the man, and entered into the swine (pigs). And the herd ran violently down a steep place into the lake, and were choked (drowned).
Those who fed them saw what was done. They fled (ran away), and went and told it in the city and in the country.

Then they went out to see what was done, and came to Jesus. They found the man, out of whom the devils (demons) had departed. He was sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed, and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
Those who saw it also told them how the man possessed of the devils (demons) was healed.

Then the whole multitude (crowd) of the country of the Gadarenes round about besought (begged) Jesus. They asked Him to depart from them, for they were taken with great fear. And Jesus went up into the ship (boat), and returned back again.
Now the man out of whom the devils (demons) had departed besought (begged) Jesus. He wanted to be with Jesus. But Jesus sent him away, saying:
Return to your own house, and show how great things God has done to you. And the man went his way. He published (told) throughout the whole city how great things Jesus had done to him.
And it came to pass (happened) when Jesus had returned. The people gladly received Him, for they were all waiting for Him.
And look, there came a man named Jairus. He was a ruler of the synagogue (meeting house). He fell down at Jesus' feet, and besought (begged) Jesus to come into his house.
For he had one only daughter, about 12 years of age, and she lay dying. But as Jesus went the people thronged (crowded) Him.
And a woman had an issue of blood (bleeding) 12 years. She had spent all her living (money) upon physicians (doctors). She could not be healed by any,
Came behind Jesus, and touched the border (edge) of His garment (clothes). And immediately her issue of blood (bleeding) stanched (stopped).
And Jesus said: Who touched Me? When all denied, Peter and they who were with him said: Master (Teacher), the multitude (crowd) throng (crowd) You and press You, and do You say: Who touched Me?
And Jesus said: Somebody has touched Me. For I perceive (know) that virtue (power) has gone out of Me.
And the woman saw that she was not hidden. She came trembling, and fell down before Him. She declared to Him before all the people why she had touched Him. She told how she was healed immediately.
And Jesus said to her: Daughter, be of good comfort (take heart). Your faith has made you whole (healed you). Go in peace.
While Jesus yet spoke, one came from the house of the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house). He said to Jairus: Your daughter is dead. Do not trouble the Master (Teacher).
But when Jesus heard it, He answered him, saying: Fear not. Believe only, and she will be made whole (healed).
And Jesus came into the house. He suffered (allowed) no man to go in, except Peter, and James, and John. Only the father and the mother of the maiden (girl) went in.
And all wept, and bewailed (cried loudly for) her. But Jesus said: Weep not. She is not dead, but sleeps.
And they laughed Him to scorn (laughed at Him), knowing that she was dead.
And Jesus put them all out, and took her by the hand, and called, saying: Maid (girl), arise (get up).
And her spirit came again, and she arose straightway (right away). And Jesus commanded to give her meat (food).
And her parents were astonished (amazed). But Jesus charged (strongly told) them that they should tell no man what was done.

verses.text: Then Jesus called His 12 disciples together. He gave them power and authority over all devils (demons), and to cure diseases.
And Jesus sent them to preach the kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
And Jesus said to them: Take nothing for your journey, neither staves (walking sticks), nor scrip (traveling bag), neither bread, neither money. Neither have 2 coats each.
And whatever house you enter into, there abide (stay), and from there depart.
And some will not receive you. When you go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet. It is for a testimony (proof) against them.
And they departed, and went through the towns, preaching the gospel (good news), and healing everywhere.
Now Herod the tetrarch (ruler over part of a land) heard of all that was done by Jesus. And he was perplexed (confused). For it was said by some that John had risen from the dead,
And by some, that Elias (Elijah) had appeared. Others said that one of the old prophets had risen again.
And Herod said: John I have beheaded (cut off the head of). But who is this, of whom I hear such things? And Herod desired (wanted) to see Jesus.
And the apostles (sent ones) returned, and told Jesus all that they had done. And He took them, and went aside privately. They went into a desert place belonging to the city called Bethsaida.
And the people knew it, and followed Jesus. And He received them, and spoke to them of the kingdom of God. He healed those who had need of healing.

And the day began to wear away. Then the 12 came, and said to Jesus: Send the multitude (crowd) away. Then they may go into the towns and country round about. They may lodge (find a place to sleep), and get victuals (food). For we are here in a desert place.
But Jesus said to them: You give them something to eat. And they said: We have no more but 5 loaves and 2 fishes. We have nothing more, unless we go and buy meat (food) for all these people.
For they were about 5,000 men. And Jesus said to His disciples: Make them sit down by fifties in a company (group).
And they did so, and made them all sit down.
Then Jesus took the 5 loaves and the 2 fishes. Looking up to heaven, He blessed them, and broke them. He gave to the disciples to set before the multitude (crowd).
And they ate, and were all filled. And there was taken up of fragments (pieces) that remained to them 12 baskets (small hand-baskets).
And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus was alone praying, His disciples were with Him. And He asked them, saying: Who do the people say that I am?
They answering said: John the Baptist. But some say: Elias (Elijah). And others say, that one of the old prophets has risen again.
Jesus said to them: But who do you say that I am? Peter answering said: The Christ of God.
And Jesus straitly charged (strongly warned) them, and commanded them to tell no man that thing,
Saying: The Son of man must suffer many things. He must be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law). He must be slain (killed), and be raised the third day.
And Jesus said to them all: If anyone will come after Me, let them deny themselves (say no to self). Let them take up their cross daily, and follow Me.
For whoever will save their life will lose it. But whoever will lose their life for My sake, the same will save it.
For what is a person advantaged (helped), if they gain the whole world? What if they lose themselves, or are cast away?

For whoever will be ashamed of Me and of My words: of them the Son of man will be ashamed. That will be when He comes in His own glory. He will come in His Father's glory, and in the glory of the holy angels.
But I tell you of a truth: There are some standing here who will not taste of death (die). They will not die till they see the kingdom of God.
And it came to pass (happened) about 8 days after these sayings. Jesus took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
And as Jesus prayed, the fashion (look) of His countenance (face) was altered (changed). His raiment (clothes) was white and glistering (shining).
And look, there talked with Him 2 men, who were Moses and Elias (Elijah),
Who appeared in glory, and spoke of His decease (death) which He would accomplish at Jerusalem.
But Peter and those with him were heavy with sleep. And when they were awake, they saw His glory. They saw the 2 men who stood with Him.

And it came to pass (happened), as the men departed from Jesus, Peter said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), it is good for us to be here. And let us make 3 tabernacles (tents): one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elias (Elijah). Peter did not know what he said.
While Peter spoke this, there came a cloud, and overshadowed (covered) them. And they feared as they entered into the cloud.
And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is My beloved (dearly loved) Son. Hear Him.
And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close (secret). In those days they told no man any of those things which they had seen.
And it came to pass (happened) on the next day. They had come down from the hill, and many people met Jesus.
And look, a man of the company cried out, saying: Master (Teacher), I beseech (beg) You, look upon my son, for he is my only child.
And look, a spirit takes him, and he suddenly cries out. And it tears (shakes) him so that he foams again. It bruises him hard, and it hardly departs from him.
And I besought (begged) Your disciples to cast him out, and they could not.
And Jesus answering said: O faithless and perverse (twisted) generation (people living now), how long will I be with you, and suffer (put up with) you? Bring your son here.

And as the boy was yet coming, the devil (demon) threw him down, and tore (shook) him. And Jesus rebuked (gave a strong command to) the unclean spirit, and healed the child. He delivered (gave) him again to his father.
And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. They all wondered at all things which Jesus did. Then He said to His disciples:
Let these sayings sink down into your ears. For the Son of man will be delivered (handed over) into the hands of men.
But they did not understand this saying. It was hidden from them, so that they did not perceive (understand) it. And they feared to ask Jesus about that saying.
Then there arose a reasoning (argument) among them, which of them should be greatest.
And Jesus, perceiving (knowing) the thought of their heart, took a child, and set him by Him,
And said to them: Whoever will receive this child in My name receives Me. And whoever will receive Me receives Him who sent Me. For the one who is least among you all, the same will be great.
And John answered and said: Master (Teacher), we saw one casting out devils (demons) in Your name. And we forbade (stopped) him, because he does not follow with us.
And Jesus said to him: Forbid him not (do not stop him). For the one who is not against us is for us.
And it came to pass (happened) when the time had come for Jesus to be received up. He stedfastly (firmly) set His face to go to Jerusalem,
And sent messengers before His face. And they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for Him.
And they did not receive Jesus. For His face was as though He would go to Jerusalem.
And His disciples James and John saw this. They said: Lord, will You have us command fire to come down from heaven? Will it consume (burn up) them, even as Elias (Elijah) did?
But Jesus turned, and rebuked (scolded) them, and said: You do not know what kind of spirit you are of.
For the Son of man has not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
And it came to pass (happened) as they went in the way. A certain man said to Jesus: Lord, I will follow You wherever You go.
And Jesus said to him: Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests. But the Son of man does not have a place to lay His head.
And Jesus said to another: Follow Me. But he said: Lord, suffer (allow) me first to go and bury my father.
Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their dead. But you go and preach the kingdom of God.
And another also said: Lord, I will follow You. But let me first go bid them farewell (say goodbye to them), who are at home at my house.
And Jesus said to him: Someone may put their hand to the plough, and look back. That one is not fit for the kingdom of God.
After these things the Lord appointed 70 others also. He sent them 2 and 2 before His face into every city and place. These were the places where He Himself would come.
Therefore Jesus said to them: The harvest truly is great, but the labourers (workers) are few. Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest, that He would send forth labourers (workers) into His harvest.
Go your ways. Look, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.
Carry neither purse (money belt), nor scrip (traveling bag), nor shoes. And salute (greet) no man by the way.
And into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace be to this house.
And if the son of peace (a person of peace) is there, your peace will rest upon it. If not, it will turn to you again.
And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give. For the labourer (worker) is worthy of their hire (pay). Go not from house to house.
And you may enter into a city, and they receive you. Then eat such things as are set before you.
And heal the sick who are there, and say to them: The kingdom of God has come nigh (near) to you.
But you may enter into a city, and they do not receive you. Then go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say:
We wipe off against you even the very dust of your city, which cleaves (sticks) on us. Notwithstanding (even so), be sure of this: The kingdom of God has come nigh (near) to you.
But I say to you: It will be more tolerable (easier) in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

Woe (great trouble) to you, Chorazin. Woe to you, Bethsaida. Mighty works have been done in you. What if they had been done in Tyre and Sidon? Those cities would have repented (changed their hearts) a great while ago. They would have sat in sackcloth (rough cloth worn when sorry) and ashes.
But it will be more tolerable (easier) for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
And you, Capernaum, which are exalted (lifted up) to heaven, will be thrust down to hell.
The one who hears you hears Me. And the one who despises (rejects) you despises Me. And the one who despises Me despises Him who sent Me.
And the 70 returned again with joy, saying: Lord, even the devils (demons) are subject (obedient) to us through Your name.
And Jesus said to them: I beheld (saw) Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
Look, I give to you power to tread (step) on serpents (snakes) and scorpions. I give you power over all the power of the enemy. And nothing will by any means hurt you.
Notwithstanding (even so), in this do not rejoice, that the spirits are subject (obedient) to you. But rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said: I thank You, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth. You have hidden these things from the wise and prudent (clever). You have revealed (shown) them to babes (little children). Even so, Father, for so it seemed good in Your sight.

All things are delivered (handed over) to Me by My Father. And no man knows who the Son is, but the Father. And no man knows who the Father is, but the Son. The one to whom the Son will reveal (show) Him knows Him too.
And Jesus turned to His disciples, and said privately: Blessed (happy) are the eyes which see the things that you see.
For I tell you: Many prophets and kings have desired (wanted) to see those things which you see. They have not seen them. They wanted to hear those things which you hear, and have not heard them.
And look, a certain lawyer (expert in God's law) stood up, and tempted (tested) Jesus, saying: Master (Teacher), what will I do to inherit (receive as my own) eternal life?
Jesus said to him: What is written in the law? How do you read it?

And the lawyer answering said: You will love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul. Love Him with all your strength, and with all your mind. And love your neighbour as yourself.
And Jesus said to him: You have answered right. Do this, and you will live.
But he, willing to justify himself (show he was right), said to Jesus: And who is my neighbour?
And Jesus answering said: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves. They stripped him of his raiment (clothes), and wounded him. They departed, leaving him half dead.
And by chance there came down a certain priest that way. And when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
And likewise a Levite (temple helper) was at the place. The Levite came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.
But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where the man was. And when he saw him, he had compassion (deep pity) on him,
The Samaritan went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine. And he set him on his own beast (animal). And he brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

And on the morrow (next day) the Samaritan departed. And he took out 2 pence (2 days' pay), and gave them to the host (inn keeper). And he said to him: Take care of him. And whatever you spend more, when I come again, I will repay you.
Which now of these 3 was neighbour to the man who fell among the thieves? What do you think?
And the lawyer said: The one who showed mercy on him. Then Jesus said to him: Go, and you do likewise.
Now it came to pass (happened), as they went, that Jesus entered into a certain village. And a certain woman named Martha received Him into her house.
And Martha had a sister called Mary. Mary also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard His word.
But Martha was cumbered (busy and worried) about much serving, and came to Jesus, and said: Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her therefore that she help me.
And Jesus answered and said to her: Martha, Martha, you are careful (full of worry) and troubled about many things.
But one thing is needful (needed). And Mary has chosen that good part, which will not be taken away from her.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened) as Jesus was praying in a certain place. When He ceased (stopped), one of His disciples said to Him: Lord, teach us to pray, as John also taught his disciples.
And Jesus said to them: When you pray, say: Our Father who is in heaven, Hallowed (holy) be Your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
Give us day by day our daily bread.
And forgive us our sins, for we also forgive every one who is indebted (owes) to us. And lead us not into temptation (testing), but deliver (rescue) us from evil.
And Jesus said to them: Suppose one of you has a friend. You go to him at midnight, and say to him: Friend, lend me 3 loaves.
For a friend of mine on his journey has come to me. And I have nothing to set before him.
And the friend from within will answer and say: Trouble me not. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I cannot rise and give you.
I say to you: The friend may not rise and give to him because he is his friend. Yet because of his importunity (not giving up when asking), he will rise. And he will give him as many as he needs.
And I say to you: Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened to you.
For every one who asks receives. And the one who seeks finds. And to the one who knocks it will be opened.
A son may ask bread of any of you who is a father. Will that father give him a stone? Or the son may ask a fish. Will the father give him a serpent (snake) for a fish?
Or if he will ask for an egg, will he offer him a scorpion?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children: How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him?

And Jesus was casting out a devil (demon), and it was dumb (could not speak). And it came to pass (happened) when the devil (demon) had gone out. The man who could not speak spoke. And the people wondered.
But some of them said: He casts out devils (demons) through Beelzebub (the devil), the chief of the devils.
And others, tempting (testing) Jesus, sought (asked) of Him a sign from heaven.
But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation (ruin). And a house divided against a house falls.
If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because you say that I cast out devils (demons) through Beelzebub (the devil).
And if I cast out devils (demons) by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But I cast out devils (demons) with the finger of God. If so, no doubt the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man armed keeps his palace, his goods are in peace.
But one stronger than he may come upon him, and overcome him. Then that one takes from him all his armour in which he trusted. And he divides his spoils (stolen goods).
The one who is not with Me is against Me. And the one who does not gather with Me scatters.
The unclean spirit may go out of a man. It walks through dry places, seeking rest. And finding none, it says: I will return to my house from which I came out.
And when it comes, it finds the house swept and garnished (decorated).
Then it goes, and takes to itself 7 other spirits more wicked than itself. And they enter in, and dwell (live) there. And the last state of that man is worse than the first.

And it came to pass (happened) as Jesus spoke these things. A certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said to Him: Blessed (happy) is the womb that bore You. Blessed are the breasts which You have sucked.
But Jesus said: Yes rather, blessed (happy) are they who hear the word of God, and keep it.

And when the people were gathered thick together, Jesus began to say: This is an evil generation (people living now). They seek a sign. And there will no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas (Jonah) the prophet.
For Jonas (Jonah) was a sign to the Ninevites. So will the Son of man also be to this generation (people living now).

The queen of the south will rise up in the judgment. She will rise with the men of this generation (people living now), and condemn (judge guilty) them. For she came from the utmost (farthest) parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. And look, a greater than Solomon is here.

The men of Nineve (Nineveh) will rise up in the judgment with this generation (people living now). They will condemn (judge guilty) it. For they repented (changed their hearts) at the preaching of Jonas (Jonah). And look, a greater than Jonas (Jonah) is here.
No man lights a candle (lamp) and puts it in a secret place. No man puts it under a bushel (basket). But a man puts it on a candlestick (lamp stand). Then those who come in may see the light.
The light of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is single (clear and focused), your whole body also is full of light. But when your eye is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
Take heed (be careful) therefore that the light which is in you is not darkness.
Your whole body may be full of light, having no part dark. Then the whole will be full of light. It will be as when the bright shining of a candle (lamp) gives you light.
And as Jesus spoke, a certain Pharisee besought (begged) Him to dine (eat) with him. And Jesus went in, and sat down to meat (to eat a meal).
And when the Pharisee saw it, he marvelled (was amazed) that Jesus had not first washed before dinner.
And the Lord said to him: Now you Pharisees make clean the outside of the cup and the platter (plate). But your inward part is full of ravening (greedy grabbing) and wickedness.
You fools. God made that which is outside. Did He not make that which is inside also?
But rather give alms (gifts to the poor) of such things as you have. And look, all things are clean to you.

But woe (great trouble) to you, Pharisees. For you tithe (give a tenth part of) mint and rue and all kinds of herbs (garden plants). But you pass over judgment (fairness) and the love of God. These you ought to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
Woe (great trouble) to you, Pharisees. For you love the uppermost (best) seats in the synagogues (meeting houses), and greetings in the markets.
Woe (great trouble) to you, scribes (teachers of the law) and Pharisees, hypocrites (pretenders). For you are as graves which do not appear. The men who walk over them are not aware of them.
Then one of the lawyers (experts in God's law) answered, and said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), saying this You reproach (insult) us also.

And Jesus said: Woe (great trouble) to you also, you lawyers (experts in God's law). For you lade (load) men with burdens (loads) grievous (hard) to be carried. And you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
Woe (great trouble) to you. For you build the sepulchres (tombs) of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
Truly you bear witness (show) that you allow (agree with) the deeds of your fathers. For they indeed killed them, and you build their sepulchres (tombs).
Therefore also the wisdom of God said: I will send them prophets and apostles (sent ones), and some of them they will slay (kill) and persecute (attack),
That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation (beginning) of the world, may be required of this generation (people living now),
From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zacharias, who perished (died) between the altar and the temple. Verily (truly) I say to you: It will be required of this generation.
Woe (great trouble) to you, lawyers (experts in God's law). For you have taken away the key of knowledge. You did not enter in yourselves, and them who were entering in you hindered (stopped).
And as Jesus said these things to them, the scribes (teachers of the law) and the Pharisees began to urge Him vehemently (hard), and to provoke Him to speak of many things,
Laying wait for Him, and seeking to catch something out of His mouth, that they might accuse Him.
