verses.text: In the meantime, when there were gathered together an innumerable (too many to count) multitude (crowd) of people, so that they trod one upon another, Jesus began to say to His disciples first of all: Beware of the leaven (yeast) of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy (pretending).
For there is nothing covered, that will not be revealed (shown), neither hidden, that will not be known.
Therefore whatever you have spoken in darkness will be heard in the light. And that which you have spoken in the ear in closets (inner rooms) will be proclaimed upon the housetops.
And I say to you My friends: Be not afraid of them who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
But I will forewarn (warn ahead of time) you whom you should fear: Fear Him, who after He has killed has power to cast into hell. Yes, I say to you, fear Him.
Are not 5 sparrows sold for 2 farthings (smallest coins), and not one of them is forgotten before God?
But even the very hairs of your head are all numbered (counted). Fear not therefore. You are of more value than many sparrows.
Also I say to you: Whoever will confess (say openly that they belong to) Me before men, them will the Son of man also confess before the angels of God.
But the one who denies (says they do not know) Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.
And whoever will speak a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven them. But to the one who blasphemes (speaks against) the Holy Spirit it will not be forgiven.
And when they bring you to the synagogues (meeting houses), and to magistrates (judges), and powers (rulers), take no thought (do not worry) how or what thing you will answer, or what you will say.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you in the same hour what you ought to say.
And one of the company said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance (family money and land) with me.
And Jesus said to him: Man, who made Me a judge or a divider over you?

And Jesus said to them: Take heed (be careful), and beware of covetousness (wanting what belongs to others). For a person's life does not consist in the abundance (large amount) of the things which they possess.
And Jesus spoke a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them, saying: The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully (very much).
And he thought within himself, saying: What will I do, because I have no room where to bestow (store) my fruits?
And he said: This I will do. I will pull down my barns, and build greater. And there I will bestow (store) all my fruits and my goods.
And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease (rest), eat, drink, and be merry (happy).
But God said to him: You fool, this night your soul will be required of you. Then whose will those things be, which you have provided?
So is the one who lays up treasure for themselves, and is not rich toward God.
And Jesus said to His disciples: Therefore I say to you, take no thought (do not worry) for your life, what you will eat, neither for the body, what you will put on.
The life is more than meat (food), and the body is more than raiment (clothes).
Consider the ravens. For they neither sow (plant) nor reap (harvest). They have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much better are you than the fowls (birds)?
And which of you by taking thought (worrying) can add to their stature (height) one cubit (about 18 inches)?
If you then are not able to do that thing which is least, why take thought (worry) for the rest?
Consider the lilies how they grow. They toil (work) not, they spin (make thread) not. And yet I say to you, that Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed (dressed) like one of these.
If then God so clothes the grass, which is today in the field, and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith?
And do not seek what you will eat, or what you will drink, neither be of doubtful (worried) mind.
For all these things the nations of the world seek after. And your Father knows that you have need of these things.
But rather seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be added to you.
Fear not, little flock. For it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

Sell what you have, and give alms (gifts to the poor). Provide yourselves bags which do not wax (grow) old, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief approaches (comes near), neither moth corrupts (eats up).
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
Let your loins (waist) be girded about (belted, ready to work), and your lights burning,
And you yourselves like men who wait for their lord (master), when he will return from the wedding, that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him immediately.

Blessed (happy) are those servants, whom the lord (master) when he comes will find watching. Verily (truly) I say to you, that he will gird (dress) himself, and make them sit down to meat (a meal), and will come forth and serve them.
And if he will come in the second watch (time of night), or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed (happy) are those servants.
And know this, that if the goodman (owner) of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered (allowed) his house to be broken through.
Be therefore ready also, for the Son of man comes at an hour when you do not think.
Then Peter said to Jesus: Lord, do You speak this parable (story that teaches a lesson) to us, or even to all?

And the Lord said: Who then is that faithful and wise steward (manager), whom his lord (master) will make ruler over his household (family), to give them their portion of meat (food) in due season (at the right time)?
Blessed (happy) is that servant, whom his lord (master) when he comes will find so doing.
Of a truth I say to you, that he will make him ruler over all that he has.
But if that servant says in his heart: My lord (master) delays his coming, and begins to beat the menservants and maidens (servant girls), and to eat and drink, and to be drunk,

The lord (master) of that servant will come in a day when he does not look for him, and at an hour when he is not aware, and will cut him in sunder (pieces), and will appoint (give) him his portion (place) with the unbelievers.
And that servant, who knew his lord's (master's) will, and did not prepare himself, neither did according to his will, will be beaten with many stripes (lashes).

But the one who did not know, and did commit things worthy of stripes (lashes), will be beaten with few stripes. For to whomever much is given, of them will much be required. And to whom men have committed (trusted) much, of them they will ask the more.
I have come to send fire on the earth. And what will I, if it is already kindled (lit)?
But I have a baptism to be baptized with. And how am I straitened (pressed hard) till it is accomplished (finished).
Do you suppose (think) that I have come to give peace on earth? I tell you: No, but rather division.
For from now on there will be 5 in one house divided, 3 against 2, and 2 against 3.

The father will be divided against the son, and the son against the father, the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother, the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.
And Jesus said also to the people: When you see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway (right away) you say: There comes a shower. And so it is.
And when you see the south wind blow, you say: There will be heat. And it comes to pass (happens).
You hypocrites (pretenders), you can discern (read) the face of the sky and of the earth. But how is it that you do not discern (understand) this time?
Yes, and why even of yourselves do you not judge what is right?

When you go with your adversary (the one taking you to court) to the magistrate (judge), as you are in the way, give diligence (work hard) that you may be delivered (set free) from him, so that he does not hale (drag) you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison.
I tell you, you will not depart from there, till you have paid the very last mite (smallest coin).

verses.text: There were present at that season (time) some who told Jesus of the Galilaeans, whose blood Pilate had mingled (mixed) with their sacrifices.
And Jesus answering said to them: Do you suppose (think) that these Galilaeans were sinners above all the Galilaeans, because they suffered such things?
I tell you: No. But, except you repent (change your hearts), you will all likewise perish (die).
Or those 18, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew (killed) them, do you think that they were sinners above all men who dwelt (lived) in Jerusalem?
I tell you: No. But, except you repent (change your hearts), you will all likewise perish (die).
Jesus spoke also this parable (story that teaches a lesson): A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard (grape farm). And he came and sought (looked for) fruit on it, and found none.
Then he said to the dresser (keeper) of his vineyard: Look, these 3 years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none. Cut it down. Why does it cumber (waste) the ground?
And the dresser answering said to him: Lord (sir), let it alone this year also, till I dig about it, and dung (fertilize) it.
And if it bears fruit, well. And if not, then after that you will cut it down.
And Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues (meeting houses) on the sabbath (day of rest).
And look, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity (sickness) 18 years, and was bowed together (bent over), and could in no way lift up herself.
And when Jesus saw her, He called her to Him, and said to her: Woman, you are loosed (set free) from your infirmity (sickness).
And Jesus laid His hands on her. And immediately she was made straight, and glorified (praised) God.

And the ruler of the synagogue (meeting house) answered with indignation (anger), because Jesus had healed on the sabbath day (day of rest), and said to the people: There are 6 days in which men ought to work. In them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day.

The Lord then answered him, and said: You hypocrite (pretender), does not each one of you on the sabbath (day of rest) loose (untie) his ox or his ass (donkey) from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, look, these 18 years, be loosed (set free) from this bond on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And when Jesus had said these things, all His adversaries (enemies) were ashamed. And all the people rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by Him.
Then Jesus said: What is the kingdom of God like? And to what will I resemble (compare) it?

It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and cast into his garden. And it grew, and waxed (grew into) a great tree. And the fowls (birds) of the air lodged (rested) in the branches of it.
And again Jesus said: To what will I liken (compare) the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven (yeast), which a woman took and hid in 3 measures of meal (flour), till the whole was leavened (raised by the yeast).
And Jesus went through the cities and villages, teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem.
Then one said to Jesus: Lord, are there few who are saved? And He said to them:
Strive (work hard) to enter in at the strait (narrow) gate. For many, I say to you, will seek to enter in, and will not be able.

When once the master of the house has risen up, and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside, and to knock at the door, saying: Lord, Lord, open to us. And he will answer and say to you: I do not know you, where you are from.
Then you will begin to say: We have eaten and drunk in your presence, and you have taught in our streets.
But he will say: I tell you, I do not know you, where you are from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity (sin).
There will be weeping and gnashing (grinding) of teeth, when you will see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves thrust out.
And they will come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and will sit down in the kingdom of God.
And look, there are last who will be first, and there are first who will be last.
The same day there came certain of the Pharisees, saying to Jesus: Get out, and depart from here, for Herod will kill You.
And Jesus said to them: Go, and tell that fox: Look, I cast out devils (demons), and I do cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I will be perfected (finished).
Nevertheless (even so) I must walk today, and tomorrow, and the day following. For it cannot be that a prophet perish (die) out of Jerusalem.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which kills the prophets, and stones them who are sent to you. How often would I have gathered your children together, as a hen gathers her brood (chicks) under her wings, and you would not.

Look, your house is left to you desolate (empty and ruined). And verily (truly) I say to you: You will not see Me, until the time comes when you will say: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.

verses.text: And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day (day of rest), that they watched Him.
And look, there was a certain man before Him who had the dropsy (a swelling sickness).
And Jesus answering spoke to the lawyers (experts in God's law) and Pharisees, saying: Is it lawful (allowed by the law) to heal on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And they held their peace (were quiet). And Jesus took the man, and healed him, and let him go,
And answered them, saying: Which of you will have an ass (donkey) or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway (right away) pull him out on the sabbath day (day of rest)?
And they could not answer Him again to these things.
And Jesus put forth a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to those who were bidden (invited), when He marked (noticed) how they chose out the chief rooms (best seats), saying to them:
When you are bidden (invited) by any man to a wedding, do not sit down in the highest room (best seat), in case a more honourable man than you is bidden by him,
And he who bade (invited) you and him comes and says to you: Give this man place. And you begin with shame to take the lowest room (seat).

But when you are bidden (invited), go and sit down in the lowest room (seat), that when he who bade you comes, he may say to you: Friend, go up higher. Then you will have worship (honor) in the presence of them who sit at meat (the meal) with you.
For whoever exalts (lifts up) himself will be abased (brought low). And the one who humbles himself will be exalted (lifted up).

Then Jesus said also to him who bade (invited) Him: When you make a dinner or a supper, do not call your friends, nor your brothers, neither your kinsmen (relatives), nor your rich neighbours, in case they also bid (invite) you again, and a recompence (repayment) is made to you.
But when you make a feast, call the poor, the maimed (people with crippled bodies), the lame (people who cannot walk well), the blind,
And you will be blessed (happy). For they cannot recompense (repay) you. For you will be recompensed at the resurrection (rising from the dead) of the just (those who are right with God).
And when one of them who sat at meat (the meal) with Jesus heard these things, he said to Him: Blessed (happy) is the one who will eat bread in the kingdom of God.
Then Jesus said to him: A certain man made a great supper, and bade (invited) many,
And sent his servant at supper time to say to them who were bidden (invited): Come, for all things are now ready.
And they all with one consent (together) began to make excuse. The first said to him: I have bought a piece of ground, and I must go and see it. I pray you have me excused.
And another said: I have bought 5 yoke (pairs) of oxen, and I go to prove (test) them. I pray you have me excused.
And another said: I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

So that servant came, and showed his lord (master) these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant: Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, and the maimed (people with crippled bodies), and the halt (crippled), and the blind.
And the servant said: Lord (master), it is done as you have commanded, and yet there is room.
And the lord (master) said to the servant: Go out into the highways (main roads) and hedges, and compel (urge) them to come in, that my house may be filled.
For I say to you, that none of those men who were bidden (invited) will taste of my supper.
And there went great multitudes (large crowds) with Jesus. And He turned, and said to them:
If anyone comes to Me, and does not hate their father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, yes, and their own life also, they cannot be My disciple.
And whoever does not bear (carry) their cross, and come after Me, cannot be My disciple.
For which of you, intending to build a tower, does not sit down first, and count the cost, whether they have enough to finish it?
Lest haply (in case), after they have laid the foundation, and are not able to finish it, all who behold (see) it begin to mock them,
Saying: This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not sit down first, and consult (think) whether he is able with 10,000 to meet him who comes against him with 20,000?
Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an ambassage (group of messengers), and desires (asks for) conditions of peace.
So likewise, whoever of you does not forsake (leave) all that they have, they cannot be My disciple.
Salt is good. But if the salt has lost its savour (taste), with what will it be seasoned?
It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill (manure pile), but men cast it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
Then all the publicans (tax collectors) and sinners drew near to Jesus to hear Him.
And the Pharisees and scribes (teachers of the law) murmured (complained), saying: This man receives sinners, and eats with them.
And Jesus spoke this parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them, saying:
What man of you, having 100 sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the 99 in the wilderness (desert), and go after that which is lost, until he finds it?
And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbours, saying to them: Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost.
I say to you, that likewise joy will be in heaven over one sinner who repents (changes their heart), more than over 99 just (right with God) persons, who need no repentance (change of heart).
Or what woman having 10 pieces of silver, if she loses one piece, does not light a candle (lamp), and sweep the house, and seek diligently (search carefully) till she finds it?
And when she has found it, she calls her friends and her neighbours together, saying: Rejoice with me, for I have found the piece which I had lost.
Likewise, I say to you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents (changes their heart).
And Jesus said: A certain man had 2 sons.
And the younger of them said to his father: Father, give me the portion (share) of goods that falls to me. And the father divided to them his living (property).
And not many days after, the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance (money) with riotous (wild) living.
And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine (time of no food) in that land, and he began to be in want (need).
And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country. And the citizen sent him into his fields to feed swine (pigs).
And he would fain (gladly) have filled his belly (stomach) with the husks that the swine (pigs) ate. And no man gave to him.
And when he came to himself, he said: How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish (am dying) with hunger.
I will arise and go to my father, and will say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before you,
And am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.
And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion (deep pity), and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
And the son said to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight, and am no more worthy to be called your son.
But the father said to his servants: Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him. And put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
And bring here the fatted calf (the calf made fat for a feast), and kill it. And let us eat, and be merry (happy).
For this my son was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry (happy).
Now his elder son was in the field. And as he came and drew nigh (near) to the house, he heard music and dancing.
And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
And the servant said to him: Your brother has come. And your father has killed the fatted calf, because he has received him safe and sound.
And the elder son was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and intreated (begged) him.

And he answering said to his father: Look, these many years I serve you, neither did I transgress (break) at any time your commandment. And yet you never gave me a kid (young goat), that I might make merry (have a party) with my friends.
But as soon as this your son had come, who has devoured (wasted) your living with harlots (prostitutes), you have killed for him the fatted calf.
And the father said to him: Son, you are ever (always) with me, and all that I have is yours.
It was meet (right) that we should make merry (be happy), and be glad. For this your brother was dead, and is alive again, and was lost, and is found.

verses.text: And Jesus said also to His disciples: There was a certain rich man, who had a steward (manager). And the same was accused to him that he had wasted his goods.
And the rich man called him, and said to him: How is it that I hear this of you? Give an account of your stewardship (managing). For you may be no longer steward (manager).
Then the steward said within himself: What will I do? For my lord (master) takes away from me the stewardship (job of managing). I cannot dig. To beg I am ashamed.
I am resolved (have decided) what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship (job), they may receive me into their houses.
So he called every one of his lord's (master's) debtors (people who owed money) to him, and said to the first: How much do you owe to my lord?
And he said: 100 measures of oil. And the steward said to him: Take your bill, and sit down quickly, and write 50.
Then he said to another: And how much do you owe? And he said: 100 measures of wheat. And the steward said to him: Take your bill, and write 80.
And the lord (master) commended (praised) the unjust steward (manager), because he had done wisely. For the children of this world are in their generation (time) wiser than the children of light.
And I say to you: Make to yourselves friends of the mammon (money) of unrighteousness (wrong), that, when you fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations (homes).
The one who is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much. And the one who is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous (wrong) mammon (money), who will commit (trust) to you the true riches?
And if you have not been faithful in that which is another man's, who will give you that which is your own?
No servant can serve 2 masters. For either he will hate the one, and love the other. Or else he will hold to the one, and despise (look down on) the other. You cannot serve God and mammon (money).
And the Pharisees also, who were covetous (loved money), heard all these things. And they derided (made fun of) Jesus.

And Jesus said to them: You are they who justify (say you are right) yourselves before men. But God knows your hearts. For that which is highly esteemed (honored) among men is abomination (hateful) in the sight of God.
The law and the prophets were until John. Since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presses (pushes hard) into it.
And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass (go away), than one tittle (smallest mark) of the law to fail.
Whoever puts away (divorces) his wife, and marries another, commits adultery (being unfaithful in marriage). And whoever marries her who is put away (divorced) from her husband commits adultery.
There was a certain rich man, who was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously (lived richly) every day.
And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, who was laid at his gate, full of sores,
And desiring (wanting) to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man's table. Moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
And it came to pass (happened), that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom (side). The rich man also died, and was buried.
And in hell he lifted up his eyes, being in torments (great pain), and sees Abraham far off, and Lazarus in his bosom (at his side).
And he cried and said: Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue. For I am tormented (in great pain) in this flame.
But Abraham said: Son, remember that you in your lifetime received your good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things. But now he is comforted, and you are tormented (in great pain).
And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf (deep gap) fixed, so that they who would pass from here to you cannot. Neither can they pass to us, who would come from there.
Then he said: I pray you therefore, father, that you would send Lazarus to my father's house,
For I have 5 brothers, that he may testify (warn) to them, so that they will not also come into this place of torment (great pain).
Abraham says to him: They have Moses and the prophets. Let them hear them.
And he said: No, father Abraham. But if one went to them from the dead, they will repent (change their hearts).
And Abraham said to him: If they do not hear Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.

verses.text: Then Jesus said to the disciples: It is impossible but that offences (things that cause sin) will come. But woe (great trouble) to the one through whom they come.
It would be better for them that a millstone (large heavy stone) were hanged about their neck, and they were cast into the sea, than that they should offend (cause to sin) one of these little ones.
Take heed (be careful) to yourselves. If your brother trespass (does wrong) against you, rebuke (correct) him. And if he repent (changes his heart), forgive him.
And if he trespass (does wrong) against you 7 times in a day, and 7 times in a day turns again to you, saying: I repent (I am sorry), you will forgive him.
And the apostles (sent ones) said to the Lord: Increase our faith.
And the Lord said: If you had faith as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this sycamine (mulberry) tree: Be plucked up by the root, and be planted in the sea. And it would obey you.
But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say to him by and by (right away), when he has come from the field: Go and sit down to meat (eat a meal)?
And will not rather say to him: Make ready that I may sup (eat supper), and gird (dress) yourself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunk. And afterward you will eat and drink?
Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow (think) not.
So likewise you, when you will have done all those things which are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable (useless) servants. We have done that which was our duty to do.
And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus went to Jerusalem, that He passed through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
And as Jesus entered into a certain village, there met Him 10 men who were lepers (people with a skin disease), who stood afar off (far away).
And they lifted up their voices, and said: Jesus, Master (Teacher), have mercy on us.
And when Jesus saw them, He said to them: Go show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass (happened), that, as they went, they were cleansed (healed).
And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified (praised) God,
And fell down on his face at Jesus' feet, giving Him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
And Jesus answering said: Were there not 10 cleansed (healed)? But where are the 9?
There are not found who returned to give glory to God, except this stranger.
And Jesus said to him: Arise (get up), go your way. Your faith has made you whole (healed you).
And when Jesus was demanded (asked) by the Pharisees, when the kingdom of God would come, He answered them and said: The kingdom of God does not come with observation (outward signs to watch).
Neither will they say: Look here, or, look there. For look, the kingdom of God is within you.
And Jesus said to the disciples: The days will come, when you will desire (want) to see one of the days of the Son of man, and you will not see it.
And they will say to you: See here, or, see there. Do not go after them, nor follow them.
For as the lightning, that lightens out of the one part under heaven, shines to the other part under heaven, so will also the Son of man be in His day.
But first He must suffer many things, and be rejected by this generation (people living now).
And as it was in the days of Noe (Noah), so will it be also in the days of the Son of man.
They ate, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe (Noah) entered into the ark (big boat), and the flood came, and destroyed them all.
Likewise also as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built.
But the same day that Lot went out of Sodom it rained fire and brimstone (burning sulfur) from heaven, and destroyed them all.
Even so will it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed (shown).
In that day, whoever will be upon the housetop, and their stuff (goods) in the house, let them not come down to take it away. And whoever is in the field, let them likewise not return back.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever will seek to save their life will lose it. And whoever will lose their life will preserve (keep) it.
I tell you, in that night there will be 2 men in one bed. The one will be taken, and the other will be left.
There will be 2 women grinding (grain) together. The one will be taken, and the other left.
There will be 2 men in the field. The one will be taken, and the other left.
And they answered and said to Jesus: Where, Lord? And He said to them: Wherever the body is, there will the eagles be gathered together.

verses.text: And Jesus spoke a parable (story that teaches a lesson) to them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint (lose heart),
Saying: There was in a city a judge, who did not fear God, neither regarded (respected) man.
And there was a widow in that city. And she came to him, saying: Avenge (give justice to) me of my adversary (enemy).
And he would not for a while. But afterward he said within himself: Though I do not fear God, nor regard (respect) man,
Yet because this widow troubles me, I will avenge (give justice to) her, so that by her continual coming she does not weary (wear out) me.
And the Lord said: Hear what the unjust judge says.
And will not God avenge (give justice to) His own elect (chosen people), who cry day and night to Him, though He bears long (is patient) with them?
I tell you that He will avenge (give justice to) them speedily (quickly). Nevertheless (but) when the Son of man comes, will He find faith on the earth?
And Jesus spoke this parable (story that teaches a lesson) to certain people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous (right with God), and despised (looked down on) others:
There were 2 men who went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican (tax collector).

The Pharisee stood and prayed this way with himself: God, I thank You, that I am not as other men are, extortioners (people who steal by force), unjust, adulterers (people unfaithful in marriage), or even as this publican (tax collector).
I fast (go without food) twice in the week. I give tithes (a tenth part) of all that I possess.
And the publican (tax collector), standing afar off (far away), would not lift up so much as his eyes to heaven, but smote (hit) upon his breast (chest), saying: God be merciful to me a sinner.

I tell you, this man went down to his house justified (made right with God) rather than the other. For every one who exalts (lifts up) himself will be abased (brought low). And the one who humbles himself will be exalted (lifted up).
And they brought to Jesus also infants (babies), that He would touch them. But when His disciples saw it, they rebuked (scolded) them.
But Jesus called them to Him, and said: Suffer (allow) little children to come to Me, and forbid them not (do not stop them). For of such is the kingdom of God.
Verily (truly) I say to you: Whoever will not receive the kingdom of God as a little child will in no way enter it.
And a certain ruler asked Jesus, saying: Good Master (Teacher), what will I do to inherit (receive as my own) eternal life?
And Jesus said to him: Why do you call Me good? None is good, except One, that is, God.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery (being unfaithful in marriage), Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness (lie about others), Honour your father and your mother.
And he said: All these I have kept from my youth up (since I was young).
Now when Jesus heard these things, He said to him: Yet you lack one thing. Sell all that you have, and distribute (give) to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. And come, follow Me.
And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful (sad), for he was very rich.
And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful (sad), He said: How hardly (with great difficulty) will they who have riches enter into the kingdom of God.
For it is easier for a camel to go through a needle's eye, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
And they who heard it said: Who then can be saved?
And Jesus said: The things which are impossible with men are possible with God.
Then Peter said: Look, we have left all, and followed You.
And Jesus said to them: Verily (truly) I say to you: There is no one who has left house, or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children, for the kingdom of God's sake,
Who will not receive manifold (many times) more in this present time, and in the world to come life everlasting.
Then Jesus took to Him the 12, and said to them: Look, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets about the Son of man will be accomplished (come true).
For He will be delivered (handed over) to the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), and will be mocked, and spitefully entreated (treated cruelly), and spit on.
And they will scourge (whip) Him, and put Him to death. And the third day He will rise again.
And they understood none of these things. And this saying was hidden from them, neither did they know the things which were spoken.
And it came to pass (happened), that as Jesus had come nigh (near) to Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the way side (road side) begging.
And hearing the multitude (crowd) pass by, he asked what it meant.
And they told him, that Jesus of Nazareth passes by.
And he cried, saying: Jesus, You Son of David, have mercy on me.
And they who went before rebuked (scolded) him, that he should hold his peace (be quiet). But he cried so much the more: You Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus stood, and commanded him to be brought to Him. And when he had come near, Jesus asked him,
Saying: What will you have Me do to you? And he said: Lord, that I may receive my sight.
And Jesus said to him: Receive your sight. Your faith has saved you.
And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus, glorifying (praising) God. And all the people, when they saw it, gave praise to God.

verses.text: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
And look, there was a man named Zacchaeus, who was the chief among the publicans (tax collectors), and he was rich.
And Zacchaeus sought (tried) to see Jesus, who He was, and could not for the press (crowd), because he was little of stature (short).
And Zacchaeus ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see Jesus, for He was to pass that way.
And when Jesus came to the place, He looked up, and saw him, and said to him: Zacchaeus, make haste (hurry), and come down. For today I must abide (stay) at your house.
And Zacchaeus made haste (hurried), and came down, and received Jesus joyfully.
And when they saw it, they all murmured (complained), saying, that Jesus had gone to be guest with a man who is a sinner.

And Zacchaeus stood, and said to the Lord: Look, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor. And if I have taken anything from any man by false accusation, I restore (pay back) him fourfold (4 times as much).
And Jesus said to him: This day salvation (saving) has come to this house, since he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man has come to seek and to save that which was lost.

And as they heard these things, Jesus added and spoke a parable (story that teaches a lesson), because He was nigh (near) to Jerusalem, and because they thought that the kingdom of God would immediately appear.
Jesus said therefore: A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
And he called his 10 servants, and delivered (gave) them 10 pounds (sums of money), and said to them: Occupy (do business) till I come.
But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying: We will not have this man to reign over us.

And it came to pass (happened), that when he had returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called to him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading.
Then came the first, saying: Lord (master), your pound has gained 10 pounds.
And he said to him: Well, you good servant. Because you have been faithful in a very little, have authority over 10 cities.
And the second came, saying: Lord (master), your pound has gained 5 pounds.
And he said likewise to him: Be you also over 5 cities.
And another came, saying: Lord (master), look, here is your pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin (cloth).
For I feared you, because you are an austere (hard and strict) man. You take up that which you did not lay down, and reap (harvest) that which you did not sow (plant).

And he says to him: Out of your own mouth will I judge you, you wicked servant. You knew that I was an austere (hard and strict) man, taking up that which I did not lay down, and reaping that which I did not sow.
Why then did you not give my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have required my own with usury (interest)?
And he said to them who stood by: Take from him the pound, and give it to him who has 10 pounds.
And they said to him: Lord (master), he has 10 pounds.
For I say to you, that to every one who has will be given. And from the one who has not, even that which they have will be taken away from them.
But those my enemies, who would not have me reign over them, bring here, and slay (kill) them before me.
And when Jesus had spoken this, He went before, ascending (going up) to Jerusalem.
And it came to pass (happened), when Jesus had come nigh (near) to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount called the mount of Olives, He sent 2 of His disciples,
Saying: Go into the village over against (across from) you, in which at your entering you will find a colt (young donkey) tied, on which no man ever yet sat. Loose (untie) him, and bring him here.
And if any man asks you: Why do you loose (untie) him? You will say this to him: Because the Lord has need of him.
And they who were sent went their way, and found even as Jesus had said to them.
And as they were loosing (untying) the colt, the owners of it said to them: Why do you loose the colt?
And they said: The Lord has need of him.
And they brought him to Jesus. And they cast their garments (clothes) upon the colt, and they set Jesus on it.
And as Jesus went, they spread their clothes in the way (road).

And when Jesus had come nigh (near), even now at the descent (way down) of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude (crowd) of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen,
Saying: Blessed be the King who comes in the name of the Lord. Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
And some of the Pharisees from among the multitude (crowd) said to Jesus: Master (Teacher), rebuke (scold) Your disciples.
And Jesus answered and said to them: I tell you that, if these should hold their peace (be quiet), the stones would immediately cry out.
And when Jesus had come near, He beheld (saw) the city, and wept over it,
Saying: If you had known, even you, at least in this your day, the things which belong to your peace. But now they are hidden from your eyes.
For the days will come upon you, that your enemies will cast a trench (dig a ditch and build a wall) about you, and compass (surround) you round, and keep you in on every side,

And will lay you even with the ground, and your children within you. And they will not leave in you one stone upon another, because you did not know the time of your visitation (when God came to you).
And Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them who sold in it, and them who bought,
Saying to them: It is written: My house is the house of prayer. But you have made it a den of thieves.
And Jesus taught daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes (teachers of the law) and the chief of the people sought (tried) to destroy Him,
And could not find what they might do. For all the people were very attentive to hear Him.

And it came to pass (happened), that on one of those days, as Jesus taught the people in the temple, and preached the gospel (good news), the chief priests and the scribes (teachers of the law) came upon Him with the elders,
And spoke to Him, saying: Tell us, by what authority do You do these things? Or who is he who gave You this authority?
And Jesus answered and said to them: I will also ask you one thing, and answer Me:
The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men?
And they reasoned with themselves, saying: If we will say: From heaven, He will say: Why then did you not believe him?
But if we say: Of men, all the people will stone us. For they are persuaded that John was a prophet.
And they answered, that they could not tell where it was from.
And Jesus said to them: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.

Then Jesus began to speak to the people this parable (story that teaches a lesson): A certain man planted a vineyard (grape farm), and let it forth (rented it) to husbandmen (farmers), and went into a far country for a long time.
And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen (farmers), that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard. But the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
And again he sent another servant. And they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully (treated him with shame), and sent him away empty.
And again he sent a third. And they wounded him also, and cast him out.
Then the lord (owner) of the vineyard said: What will I do? I will send my beloved (dearly loved) son. It may be they will reverence (respect) him when they see him.
But when the husbandmen (farmers) saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying: This is the heir (the one who will own it all). Come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be ours.
So they cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. What therefore will the lord (owner) of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy these husbandmen (farmers), and will give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said: God forbid (may it never be).
And Jesus beheld (looked at) them, and said: What is this then that is written: The stone which the builders rejected, the same has become the head of the corner (the most important stone)?
Whoever will fall upon that stone will be broken. But on whomever it will fall, it will grind them to powder.

And the chief priests and the scribes (teachers of the law) the same hour sought (tried) to lay hands on Jesus, and they feared the people. For they perceived (knew) that He had spoken this parable against them.

And they watched Jesus, and sent forth spies, who should feign (pretend) themselves just (good) men, that they might take hold of His words, that so they might deliver (hand over) Him to the power and authority of the governor.
And they asked Him, saying: Master (Teacher), we know that You say and teach rightly, neither do You accept the person of any (favor anyone), but teach the way of God truly.
Is it lawful (allowed by the law) for us to give tribute (tax) to Caesar, or no?
But Jesus perceived (saw) their craftiness (trickery), and said to them: Why do you tempt (test) Me?
Show Me a penny (a coin worth a day's pay). Whose image (picture) and superscription (writing) does it have? They answered and said: Caesar's.
And Jesus said to them: Render (give) therefore to Caesar the things which are Caesar's, and to God the things which are God's.
And they could not take hold of His words before the people. And they marvelled (were amazed) at His answer, and held their peace (were quiet).
Then came to Jesus certain of the Sadducees, who deny that there is any resurrection (rising from the dead). And they asked Him,

Saying: Master (Teacher), Moses wrote to us: If any man's brother dies, having a wife, and he dies without children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise up seed (children) to his brother.
There were therefore 7 brothers. And the first took a wife, and died without children.
And the second took her as wife, and he died childless.
And the third took her. And in the same way the 7 also. And they left no children, and died.
Last of all the woman died also.
Therefore in the resurrection (rising from the dead) whose wife of them is she? For 7 had her as wife.
And Jesus answering said to them: The children of this world marry, and are given in marriage.
But they who will be accounted (counted) worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection (rising) from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage.
Neither can they die any more. For they are equal to the angels, and are the children of God, being the children of the resurrection (rising from the dead).
Now that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
For He is not a God of the dead, but of the living. For all live to Him.
Then certain of the scribes (teachers of the law) answering said: Master (Teacher), You have well said.
And after that they durst (dared) not ask Him any question at all.
And Jesus said to them: How do they say that Christ is David's son?
And David himself says in the book of Psalms: The LORD said to my Lord: Sit on My right hand,
Till I make Your enemies Your footstool (a place to rest Your feet).
David therefore calls Him Lord. How is He then his son?
Then in the audience (hearing) of all the people Jesus said to His disciples:

Beware of the scribes (teachers of the law), who desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the markets, and the highest seats in the synagogues (meeting houses), and the chief rooms (best places) at feasts,
Who devour (eat up) widows' houses, and for a show make long prayers. The same will receive greater damnation (punishment).

verses.text: And Jesus looked up, and saw the rich men casting their gifts into the treasury (temple money box).
And Jesus saw also a certain poor widow casting in there 2 mites (smallest coins).
And Jesus said: Of a truth I say to you, that this poor widow has cast in more than they all.
For all these have of their abundance (extra) cast in to the offerings of God. But she of her penury (being poor) has cast in all the living (money to live on) that she had.
And as some spoke of the temple, how it was adorned (decorated) with goodly (beautiful) stones and gifts, Jesus said:
As for these things which you behold (see), the days will come, in which there will not be left one stone upon another, that will not be thrown down.
And they asked Jesus, saying: Master (Teacher), but when will these things be? And what sign will there be when these things will come to pass (happen)?
And Jesus said: Take heed (be careful) that you are not deceived (fooled). For many will come in My name, saying: I am Christ. And the time draws near. Do not go therefore after them.
But when you will hear of wars and commotions (riots), be not terrified. For these things must first come to pass (happen). But the end is not by and by (right away).
Then Jesus said to them: Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
And great earthquakes will be in divers (many different) places, and famines (times of no food), and pestilences (deadly sicknesses). And fearful sights and great signs will there be from heaven.

But before all these, they will lay their hands on you, and persecute (attack) you, delivering (handing) you up to the synagogues (meeting houses), and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for My name's sake.
And it will turn to you for a testimony (a chance to tell about Me).
Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before (plan ahead) what you will answer.
For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries (enemies) will not be able to gainsay (argue against) nor resist.
And you will be betrayed both by parents, and brothers, and kinsfolks (relatives), and friends. And some of you they will cause to be put to death.
And you will be hated by all men for My name's sake.
But there will not a hair of your head perish (be lost).
In your patience possess (keep) your souls.
And when you will see Jerusalem compassed (surrounded) with armies, then know that the desolation (ruin) of it is nigh (near).
Then let them who are in Judaea flee (run away) to the mountains. And let them who are in the middle of it depart out. And let not them who are in the countries (fields) enter into it.
For these are the days of vengeance (punishment), that all things which are written may be fulfilled (come true).

But woe (great trouble) to them who are with child (pregnant), and to them who give suck (nurse babies), in those days. For there will be great trouble in the land, and wrath (anger) upon this people.

And they will fall by the edge of the sword, and will be led away captive (as prisoners) into all nations. And Jerusalem will be trodden down by the Gentiles (people who are not Jews), until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled (finished).
And there will be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars. And upon the earth trouble of nations, with perplexity (confusion), the sea and the waves roaring,
Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth. For the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
And when these things begin to come to pass (happen), then look up, and lift up your heads. For your redemption (being bought back and set free) draws nigh (near).
And Jesus spoke to them a parable (story that teaches a lesson): Behold (look at) the fig tree, and all the trees.
When they now shoot forth (put out leaves), you see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh (near) at hand.
So likewise you, when you see these things come to pass (happen), know that the kingdom of God is nigh (near) at hand.
Verily (truly) I say to you: This generation (people living now) will not pass away, till all is fulfilled (has come true).
Heaven and earth will pass away. But My words will not pass away.

And take heed (be careful) to yourselves, so that at no time your hearts are overcharged (weighed down) with surfeiting (eating and drinking too much), and drunkenness, and cares (worries) of this life, and so that day comes upon you unawares (by surprise).
For as a snare (trap) it will come on all them who dwell (live) on the face of the whole earth.
Watch therefore, and pray always, that you may be accounted (counted) worthy to escape all these things that will come to pass (happen), and to stand before the Son of man.
And in the day time Jesus was teaching in the temple. And at night He went out, and abode (stayed) in the mount that is called the mount of Olives.
And all the people came early in the morning to Jesus in the temple, to hear Him.

verses.text: Now the feast of unleavened bread (bread made without yeast) drew nigh (near), which is called the Passover (feast of freedom from Egypt).
And the chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law) sought (looked for a way) how they might kill Jesus, for they feared the people.
Then Satan entered into Judas surnamed (also called) Iscariot, being of the number of the 12.
And Judas went his way, and communed (talked) with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray (hand over) Jesus to them.
And they were glad, and covenanted (agreed) to give him money.
And Judas promised, and sought opportunity (looked for a chance) to betray (hand over) Jesus to them in the absence of the multitude (crowd).
Then came the day of unleavened bread (bread made without yeast), when the passover (lamb) must be killed.
And Jesus sent Peter and John, saying: Go and prepare us the passover (meal), that we may eat.
And they said to Him: Where will You have us prepare?
And Jesus said to them: Look, when you have entered into the city, there will a man meet you, bearing (carrying) a pitcher of water. Follow him into the house where he enters in.
And you will say to the goodman (owner) of the house: The Master (Teacher) says to you: Where is the guestchamber (guest room), where I will eat the passover with My disciples?
And he will show you a large upper room furnished. There make ready.
And they went, and found as Jesus had said to them. And they made ready the passover.
And when the hour had come, Jesus sat down, and the 12 apostles (sent ones) with Him.
And Jesus said to them: With desire I have desired (I have wanted very much) to eat this passover with you before I suffer.
For I say to you, I will not any more eat of it, until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
And Jesus took the cup, and gave thanks, and said: Take this, and divide it among yourselves.
For I say to you, I will not drink of the fruit of the vine, until the kingdom of God will come.
And Jesus took bread, and gave thanks, and broke it, and gave to them, saying: This is My body which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of Me.
Likewise also the cup after supper, saying: This cup is the new testament (new agreement) in My blood, which is shed for you.
But look, the hand of him who betrays (hands over) Me is with Me on the table.
And truly the Son of man goes, as it was determined (planned). But woe (great trouble) to that man by whom He is betrayed (handed over).
And they began to enquire (ask) among themselves, which of them it was who would do this thing.
And there was also a strife (argument) among them, which of them should be accounted (counted) the greatest.
And Jesus said to them: The kings of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews) exercise lordship (rule) over them. And they who exercise authority upon them are called benefactors (people who do good).
But you will not be so. But the one who is greatest among you, let them be as the younger. And the one who is chief (leader), as the one who serves.
For which is greater, the one who sits at meat (the meal), or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at meat? But I am among you as the one who serves.
You are they who have continued with Me in My temptations (testings).
And I appoint (give) to you a kingdom, as My Father has appointed to Me,
That you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the 12 tribes of Israel.
And the Lord said: Simon, Simon, look, Satan has desired (asked) to have you, that he may sift (shake) you as wheat.
But I have prayed for you, that your faith will not fail. And when you are converted (turned back), strengthen your brothers.
And Peter said to Him: Lord, I am ready to go with You, both into prison, and to death.
And Jesus said: I tell you, Peter, the cock (rooster) will not crow this day, before you will thrice (3 times) deny (say you do not know) that you know Me.
And Jesus said to them: When I sent you without purse (money belt), and scrip (traveling bag), and shoes, did you lack anything? And they said: Nothing.

Then Jesus said to them: But now, the one who has a purse (money belt), let them take it, and likewise their scrip (traveling bag). And the one who has no sword, let them sell their garment (coat), and buy one.

For I say to you, that this that is written must yet be accomplished (come true) in Me: And He was reckoned (counted) among the transgressors (lawbreakers). For the things about Me have an end (are coming true).
And they said: Lord, look, here are 2 swords. And Jesus said to them: It is enough.
And Jesus came out, and went, as He was wont (used to do), to the mount of Olives. And His disciples also followed Him.
And when Jesus was at the place, He said to them: Pray that you do not enter into temptation (testing).
And Jesus was withdrawn from them about a stone's cast (as far as a stone can be thrown), and kneeled down, and prayed,
Saying: Father, if You are willing, remove this cup from Me. Nevertheless (but) not My will, but Yours, be done.
And there appeared an angel to Jesus from heaven, strengthening Him.
And being in an agony (great pain and struggle) Jesus prayed more earnestly (strongly). And His sweat was as it were great drops of blood falling down to the ground.
And when Jesus rose up from prayer, and had come to His disciples, He found them sleeping for sorrow (sadness),
And said to them: Why do you sleep? Rise and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation (testing).
And while Jesus yet spoke, look, a multitude (crowd), and he who was called Judas, one of the 12, went before them, and drew near to Jesus to kiss Him.
But Jesus said to him: Judas, do you betray (hand over) the Son of man with a kiss?
When they who were about Jesus saw what would follow, they said to Him: Lord, will we smite (strike) with the sword?
And one of them smote (struck) the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
And Jesus answered and said: Suffer (allow) this far. And Jesus touched his ear, and healed him.
Then Jesus said to the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, who had come to Him: Have you come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves (clubs)?
When I was daily with you in the temple, you stretched forth no hands against Me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
Then they took Jesus, and led Him, and brought Him into the high priest's house. And Peter followed afar off (far behind).
And when they had kindled (lit) a fire in the middle of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
But a certain maid (servant girl) beheld (saw) Peter as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said: This man was also with Him.
And Peter denied Him, saying: Woman, I do not know Him.
And after a little while another saw him, and said: You are also of them. And Peter said: Man, I am not.
And about the space of one hour after, another confidently affirmed (said strongly), saying: Of a truth this fellow also was with Him, for he is a Galilaean.
And Peter said: Man, I do not know what you say. And immediately, while he yet spoke, the cock (rooster) crowed.
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how He had said to him: Before the cock (rooster) crows, you will deny Me thrice (3 times).
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
And the men who held Jesus mocked Him, and smote (struck) Him.
And when they had blindfolded Him, they struck Him on the face, and asked Him, saying: Prophesy (tell us by God's power), who is it who smote (struck) You?
And many other things they spoke blasphemously (with words against God) against Him.
And as soon as it was day, the elders of the people and the chief priests and the scribes (teachers of the law) came together, and led Jesus into their council (Jewish court), saying:
Are You the Christ? Tell us. And Jesus said to them: If I tell you, you will not believe.
And if I also ask you, you will not answer Me, nor let Me go.
Hereafter (from now on) the Son of man will sit on the right hand of the power of God.
Then they all said: Are You then the Son of God? And Jesus said to them: You say that I am.
And they said: What need do we have of any further witness? For we ourselves have heard from His own mouth.

verses.text: And the whole multitude (crowd) of them arose, and led Jesus to Pilate.
And they began to accuse Him, saying: We found this fellow perverting (turning away) the nation, and forbidding to give tribute (tax) to Caesar, saying that He Himself is Christ a King.
And Pilate asked Him, saying: Are You the King of the Jews? And Jesus answered him and said: You say it.
Then Pilate said to the chief priests and to the people: I find no fault in this man.
And they were the more fierce, saying: He stirs up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry (the land of the Jews), beginning from Galilee to this place.
When Pilate heard of Galilee, he asked whether the man were a Galilaean.
And as soon as Pilate knew that Jesus belonged to Herod's jurisdiction (area of rule), he sent Him to Herod, who himself also was at Jerusalem at that time.

And when Herod saw Jesus, he was exceeding (very) glad. For he was desirous (wanting) to see Him of a long season (time), because he had heard many things of Him. And he hoped to have seen some miracle done by Him.
Then Herod questioned with Jesus in many words. But Jesus answered him nothing.
And the chief priests and scribes (teachers of the law) stood and vehemently (strongly) accused Him.
And Herod with his men of war (soldiers) set Jesus at nought (treated Him as nothing), and mocked Him, and arrayed (dressed) Him in a gorgeous robe, and sent Him again to Pilate.
And the same day Pilate and Herod were made friends together. For before they were at enmity (hate) between themselves.
And Pilate, when he had called together the chief priests and the rulers and the people,

Said to them: You have brought this man to me, as one who perverts (turns away) the people. And look, I, having examined Him before you, have found no fault in this man touching (about) those things of which you accuse Him.
No, nor yet Herod. For I sent you to him, and look, nothing worthy of death is done to Him.
I will therefore chastise (whip) Him, and release Him.
For of necessity Pilate must release one to them at the feast.
And they cried out all at once, saying: Away with this man, and release to us Barabbas,
Who for a certain sedition (riot against the rulers) made in the city, and for murder, was cast into prison.
Pilate therefore, willing to release Jesus, spoke again to them.
But they cried, saying: Crucify Him, crucify Him.
And Pilate said to them the third time: Why, what evil has He done? I have found no cause of death in Him. I will therefore chastise (whip) Him, and let Him go.
And they were instant (kept pressing) with loud voices, requiring (demanding) that He might be crucified. And the voices of them and of the chief priests prevailed (won).
And Pilate gave sentence that it should be as they required (demanded).
And Pilate released to them him who for sedition (riot against the rulers) and murder was cast into prison, whom they had desired (asked for). But he delivered (handed over) Jesus to their will.
And as they led Jesus away, they laid hold upon one Simon, a Cyrenian, coming out of the country, and on him they laid the cross, that he might bear (carry) it after Jesus.
And there followed Jesus a great company of people, and of women, who also bewailed (cried loudly) and lamented (mourned for) Him.
But Jesus turning to them said: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for Me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children.
For look, the days are coming, in which they will say: Blessed (happy) are the barren (women who cannot have children), and the wombs that never bore, and the breasts which never gave suck (nursed).
Then they will begin to say to the mountains: Fall on us. And to the hills: Cover us.
For if they do these things in a green tree, what will be done in the dry?
And there were also 2 others, malefactors (evildoers), led with Jesus to be put to death.
And when they had come to the place, which is called Calvary (the Skull), there they crucified Jesus, and the malefactors (evildoers), one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
Then Jesus said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. And they parted (divided) His raiment (clothes), and cast lots (gambled).
And the people stood beholding (watching). And the rulers also with them derided (made fun of) Him, saying: He saved others. Let Him save Himself, if He is Christ, the chosen of God.
And the soldiers also mocked Him, coming to Him, and offering Him vinegar,
And saying: If You are the king of the Jews, save Yourself.
And a superscription (sign) also was written over Him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And one of the malefactors (evildoers) who were hanged railed on (insulted) Jesus, saying: If You are Christ, save Yourself and us.
But the other answering rebuked (scolded) him, saying: Do you not fear God, seeing you are in the same condemnation (punishment)?
And we indeed justly (fairly), for we receive the due reward of our deeds. But this man has done nothing amiss (wrong).
And he said to Jesus: Lord, remember me when You come into Your kingdom.
And Jesus said to him: Verily (truly) I say to you: Today you will be with Me in paradise.
And it was about the sixth hour (noon), and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour (3 p.m.).
And the sun was darkened, and the veil (curtain) of the temple was rent (torn) in the middle.
And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, He said: Father, into Your hands I commend (give) My spirit. And having said this, He gave up the ghost (died).
Now when the centurion (army officer) saw what was done, he glorified (praised) God, saying: Certainly this was a righteous (good and right) man.
And all the people who came together to that sight, beholding (seeing) the things which were done, smote (beat) their breasts (chests), and returned.
And all His acquaintance (friends), and the women who followed Him from Galilee, stood afar off (far away), beholding (watching) these things.
And look, there was a man named Joseph, a counsellor (member of the Jewish court). And he was a good man, and a just (right with God) man.
The same had not consented (agreed) to the counsel (plan) and deed of them. He was of Arimathaea, a city of the Jews, who also himself waited for the kingdom of God.
This man went to Pilate, and begged the body of Jesus.
And Joseph took it down, and wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a sepulchre (tomb) that was hewn (cut) in stone, in which no man was ever laid before.
And that day was the preparation (day to get ready), and the sabbath (day of rest) drew on (was beginning).
And the women also, who came with Jesus from Galilee, followed after, and beheld (saw) the sepulchre (tomb), and how His body was laid.
And they returned, and prepared spices and ointments (perfumed oils). And they rested the sabbath day (day of rest) according to the commandment.
Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the sepulchre (tomb), bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.
And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre (tomb).
And they entered in, and did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
And it came to pass (happened), as they were much perplexed (confused) about this, look, 2 men stood by them in shining garments (clothes).
And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, the men said to them: Why do you seek (look for) the living among the dead?
He is not here, but is risen. Remember how He spoke to you when He was yet in Galilee,
Saying: The Son of man must be delivered (handed over) into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.
And they remembered His words,
And returned from the sepulchre (tomb), and told all these things to the 11, and to all the rest.
It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women who were with them, who told these things to the apostles (sent ones).
And their words seemed to them as idle tales (nonsense), and they did not believe them.

Then Peter arose, and ran to the sepulchre (tomb). And stooping down, he beheld (saw) the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which had come to pass (happened).
And look, 2 of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs (about 7 miles).
And they talked together of all these things which had happened.
And it came to pass (happened), that, while they communed (talked) together and reasoned, Jesus Himself drew near, and went with them.
But their eyes were holden (held back) that they should not know Him.
And Jesus said to them: What kind of communications (talk) are these that you have one to another, as you walk, and are sad?
And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said to Him: Are You only a stranger in Jerusalem, and have not known the things which have come to pass there in these days?
And Jesus said to them: What things? And they said to Him: About Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered (handed over) Him to be condemned (judged guilty) to death, and have crucified Him.
But we trusted that it had been He who should have redeemed (bought back and set free) Israel. And beside all this, today is the third day since these things were done.
Yes, and certain women also of our company made us astonished (amazed), who were early at the sepulchre (tomb).
And when they did not find His body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, who said that He was alive.
And certain of them who were with us went to the sepulchre (tomb), and found it even so as the women had said. But Him they did not see.
Then Jesus said to them: O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken.
Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into His glory?
And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, Jesus expounded (explained) to them in all the scriptures the things about Himself.
And they drew nigh (near) to the village, where they went. And Jesus made as though He would have gone further.
But they constrained (urged) Him, saying: Abide (stay) with us, for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And Jesus went in to tarry (stay) with them.
And it came to pass (happened), as Jesus sat at meat (the meal) with them, He took bread, and blessed it, and broke, and gave to them.
And their eyes were opened, and they knew Him. And He vanished out of their sight.
And they said one to another: Did not our heart burn within us, while He talked with us by the way, and while He opened to us the scriptures?
And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the 11 gathered together, and them who were with them,
Saying: The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon.
And they told what things were done in the way, and how Jesus was known by them in breaking of bread.
And as they spoke this, Jesus Himself stood in the middle of them, and says to them: Peace be to you.
But they were terrified and affrighted (scared), and supposed (thought) that they had seen a spirit.
And Jesus said to them: Why are you troubled? And why do thoughts arise in your hearts?
Behold (look at) My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself. Handle (touch) Me, and see. For a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see Me have.
And when Jesus had spoken this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
And while they yet did not believe for joy, and wondered, Jesus said to them: Do you have here any meat (food)?
And they gave Him a piece of a broiled fish, and of a honeycomb.
And Jesus took it, and ate before them.

And Jesus said to them: These are the words which I spoke to you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled (come true), which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, about Me.
Then Jesus opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures,
And said to them: Thus it is written, and thus it behoved (was needed for) Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day,
And that repentance (a change of heart) and remission (forgiveness) of sins should be preached in His name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
And you are witnesses of these things.
And look, I send the promise of My Father upon you. But tarry (stay) in the city of Jerusalem, until you are endued (clothed) with power from on high.
And Jesus led them out as far as to Bethany, and He lifted up His hands, and blessed them.
And it came to pass (happened), while Jesus blessed them, He was parted from them, and carried up into heaven.
And they worshipped Him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
And were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
